recipes.source_note: handwritten recipe card (on Crazy Cake card)
recipes.description: Quick-cooked fudge frosting to pour over Crazy Cake with peanut butter.

instructions.text: Combine sugar, cocoa, milk, butter, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a full boil.
Boil for 1½ minutes (or 3 minutes for thicker fudge).
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and beat to spreading consistency.
Pour over peanut butter layer on cake while still warm.

notes: Pour over peanut butter layer while frosting is still pourable
Double recipe and cook 3 minutes for standalone fudge

recipes.title: No Bake Oatmeal Fudge Cookies
recipes.description: Classic no-bake cookies with chocolate, peanut butter, and oatmeal. Labeled as the 'Best recipe'!

instructions.text: Combine sugar, milk, cocoa, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil and boil for 1 minute (or to soft ball stage).
Remove from heat.
Add butter, oatmeal, peanut butter, and vanilla.
Mix until well blended.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto wax paper.
Let cool and set before serving.

notes: Labeled 'Best recipe' on original card
Crunchy peanut butter adds texture
Work quickly - mixture sets fast

recipes.title: Shortbread Cookies
recipes.description: Classic 3-ingredient shortbread cookies - simple and buttery.

instructions.text: Mix soft butter with sugar until well combined.
Stir in flour and mix well.
Chill dough until firm.
Roll out to ⅓ inch thickness.
Cut out cookies with desired shapes.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) for 20 minutes. Do not let brown.

notes: Low temperature prevents browning for traditional pale shortbread
Add ¼ tsp baking powder if making into pop tarts

recipes.title: Johnny Cake
recipes.description: Traditional cornmeal quick bread, also known as johnnycake or journey cake.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a 9-inch square pan.
Mix dry ingredients together (cornmeal, flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, soda).
Cut in lard until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Beat egg with sour milk.
Add wet ingredients to dry and stir just until combined.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25-30 minutes until golden.

notes: Traditional New England/Southern quick bread
Sour milk = buttermilk or milk with 1 tbsp vinegar

recipes.title: French Onion Soup
recipes.description: Classic French onion soup with caramelized onions, beef broth, and Gruyère cheese.

instructions.text: In heavy 4- to 6-quart pot, melt butter; add oil.
Stir in onions; cover and cook 15 minutes until onions are completely wilted.
Uncover pot; stir in salt, sugar, and pepper.
Increase heat to moderately high. Cook onions 30 to 40 minutes, stirring every 2-3 minutes and scraping bottom of pot until onions are nutty brown.
Sprinkle browned onions with flour and stir thoroughly until smooth.
Slowly pour in 2 cans of the broth, stirring constantly.
When well blended, add remaining broth and wine; partially cover pot and simmer over moderately low heat for 1½ hours.
May be refrigerated and later reheated.
To serve: Ladle into 6 heat-proof bowls. Arrange thin slice of French bread on top of each and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in preheated 375°F (190°C) oven for 20 minutes.
Then broil for 3-5 minutes until cheese is lightly browned.

notes: Proper caramelization of onions is key - don't rush it
Can make soup ahead and reheat

recipes.title: Rick's French Onion Soup
recipes.description: Crock pot version of French onion soup for easy preparation.

instructions.text: In large skillet, cook onions in butter until lightly browned. (Allow enough preparation time for this.)
In crock pot, combine browned onions with cooking butter, bouillon, water, Worcestershire sauce, and salt.
Cover; cook on low for 4 to 5½ hours.
Place 3 slices of Swiss cheese on top of the liquid in the crock pot.
Cook 20 to 30 minutes more.
Add a few more Swiss cheese slices shortly before serving.
Place slices of toasted French bread in 4 soup bowls.
Top each with a slice of cold Swiss cheese.
Stir soup in crock pot and ladle over bread. Serve immediately.

notes: Recipe may be doubled and kept hot in slow-cooking pot
The layering of cheese at different stages creates great texture

recipes.title: Chicken and Cabbage Panade
recipes.description: Layered casserole of chicken, cabbage, bread, and cheese - a panade is a bread-thickened dish.

ingredients.prep_note: boneless, skinless, cut into thin strips

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium-high heat (add a little oil, less butter to prevent scorching, or substitute margarine).
Add cabbage, carrots, onions and raw chicken. Cook and stir until vegetables are tender and chicken no longer pink.
Place 4 slices of French bread in bottom of ungreased 2½- to 3-quart casserole.
Spoon half of cabbage mixture over bread; sprinkle with 1 tablespoon of the Parmesan cheese.
Repeat with 4 slices of bread, remaining cabbage mixture and 1 tablespoon of the Parmesan.
Top with remaining bread. Pour chicken broth over bread and cabbage mixture.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with Swiss cheese and remaining 1 tablespoon Parmesan.
Bake 20-25 minutes more or until edges are bubbly.
Serve in soup bowls with knife, fork and spoon for each diner.

notes: A panade is a traditional bread-based casserole
Serve with utensils - it's a knife-and-fork dish

recipes.title: Crispy Parmesan Tenders
recipes.description: Crispy baked chicken tenders coated in Parmesan and buttery crackers.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and spray with non-stick cooking spray.
Rinse chicken with cold water and pat dry with paper towels.
Pour oil into a shallow dish.
In a separate shallow dish, combine finely crushed cracker crumbs, Parmesan, and garlic powder.
Dip chicken tenderloins (or chicken breasts cut into long portions) into the oil one at a time, letting excess drip back into dish.
Roll each piece in the crumb mixture.
Arrange coated tenderloins in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes or until done.
Serve chicken strips with a dipping sauce of choice, such as Kraft's bottled sweet & sour sauce.

notes: The only recipe not from the new Pillsbury cookbook mentioned in the article
Great kid-friendly dinner

recipes.title: Chinese Chicken Tacos
recipes.description: Asian-inspired tacos with ginger-soy chicken and cabbage.

instructions.text: Spray a large non-stick skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Heat over medium-high heat until hot.
Add chicken, ginger and garlic. Cook and stir 3 to 5 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Reduce heat to low.
Add soy sauce, honey, green onion and crushed red pepper flakes; stir to coat.
Cover; cook over low heat for 5 minutes, or until chicken is no longer pink, stirring occasionally.
To serve, place scant ¼ cup chicken in each taco shell, and tuck in lots of shredded iceberg lettuce or napa cabbage.

notes: Menu suggestion: Serve two or three tacos per dinner plate with egg drop soup topped with lots of green onion slices and a scoop of hot rice mixed with tiny thawed peas, a pinch of golden turmeric or curry powder and a spoonful of sweet & sour dressing or bottled sweet & sour sauce.

recipes.title: Brown Sugar Apple Crumb Pie
recipes.source_note: newspaper clipping (from The Artful Pie: Unforgettable Recipes for Creative Cooks, 1993)
recipes.description: Double-crust apple pie with a brown sugar crumb crust and buttery topping.

ingredients.prep_note: firm, tart, will hold shape when baked
cut into small pieces, for crust
cut into small pieces, for topping

instructions.text: For filling: In a large, non-aluminum saucepan, stir together the lemon juice, water and brown sugar.
Peel, core and slice the apples. Stir the apples into the lemon and sugar mixture.
Stir in the raisins. Place the saucepan over medium heat and cook until the apples are tender, about 5 to 6 minutes. Stir them occasionally and gently as they cook.
For crumb crust: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Thoroughly butter the sides and bottom of a 10-inch pie pan.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the all-purpose flour, whole-wheat flour, brown sugar and salt.

Use a pastry blender to cut the butter into the dry ingredients until the butter pieces are the size of small peas. This may also be done in an electric mixer on the lowest speed, but be careful not to overmix.
Cut the egg yolk into the crumb mixture until it is evenly distributed.
Assembly and baking: Set aside 1 cup of the crumb mixture.
Press the remaining crumb mixture into the bottom and sides of the prepared pie pan.
Spoon the apples into the crumb-lined pan and pat them down lightly.
Sprinkle the reserved cup of crumbs over the apples.
Dot the top of the pie with the butter pieces.
Bake until bubbling and brown on top, 50 to 55 minutes.
Serve warm or cool.

notes: From The Artful Pie cookbook (Chapters, 1993; $24.95)
Use firm tart apples that hold their shape

recipes.title: Creamy Linguini with Bacon and Peas
recipes.attribution: Charlotte Balcomb Lane, Knight-Ridder News Service
recipes.description: Creamy pasta with bacon, peas, and Parmesan in a light evaporated milk sauce.

instructions.text: Cook the pasta according to package directions. When tender, drain thoroughly and set aside.
While the pasta is cooking, fry the bacon over medium heat in a large nonstick skillet until crisp and brown.
Remove the bacon to paper towels and blot thoroughly.
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the grease. (You may discard all the bacon grease and substitute 1 tablespoon olive or corn oil in its place.)
Cook the onion, garlic and mushrooms in the grease or oil until the vegetables are soft and slightly brown, about 5 minutes.
Remove the vegetables from the skillet and set aside.
In a small dish, combine the flour, salt, basil, white pepper and nutmeg.
Add the 1 teaspoon of olive oil to the skillet and heat over medium-low heat.
Sprinkle the flour mixture over the oil and stir with a wire whisk or a slotted spoon for 1 minute until the flour is slightly toasted in the oil.
Pour the evaporated skim milk into the skillet, stirring constantly to prevent lumps from forming. (If lumps form, don't worry, just keep stirring.)
Cook until the mixture comes to a boil and thickens.
Stir the bacon and vegetables into the sauce, then add the peas, lemon juice and Parmesan cheese.
Cook over low heat 2-3 minutes, then stir in the cooked pasta.
If sauce is too thick, thin with 1-2 tablespoons of water or regular skim milk.

notes: Nutritional information per serving: 304 calories, 8.5 gm. fat (25% of calories from fat), 12 gm. protein, 46 gm. carbohydrate, 6 mg. cholesterol, 338 mg. sodium

recipes.title: Vidalia Onion Dip
recipes.attribution: 1989 Vidalia Onion Cookoff Grand Prize Winner
recipes.description: Award-winning sweet onion dip - grand prize winner at the 1989 Vidalia Onion Cookoff.

instructions.text: Peel and thinly slice the onions.
Soak for 2 to 4 hours in the sugar, vinegar, and water mixture.
Drain well.
Toss with mayonnaise and celery salt.
Serve on saltine crackers. Also great with hot dogs and hamburgers.

notes: Grand Prize Winner - 1989 Vidalia Onion Cookoff, Glennville, GA
The sugar-vinegar soak mellows the onions

recipes.title: Vidalia Onion Classic Casserole
recipes.description: Creamy Vidalia onion casserole with sherry and two cheeses.

instructions.text: Sauté sweet onions in butter until they are transparent.
Add chicken broth, sherry and flour. Cook and stir until slightly thickened.
Transfer to a medium casserole.
Top with bread crumbs and both cheeses.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 20 to 30 minutes or until lightly browned and bubbly.
May be prepared ahead of time and refrigerated, then baked.

notes: Can be made ahead and refrigerated before baking

recipes.title: Vidalia Cheese Wafer
recipes.description: Sharp cheddar cheese crackers with Vidalia onion and a hint of cayenne.

instructions.text: In large mixing bowl, blend grated Cheddar with flour, Parmesan, seasoned salt, butter (cut in bits), diced sweet onion and cayenne.
Blend well by beating with a wooden spoon or mixer.
Form dough into two rolls; wrap in plastic wrap.
Place in freezer 30 minutes or fridge for a couple of hours.
Slice into wafers about ¼-inch thick.
Space close together, but not touching, on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake one sheet at a time at 375°F (190°C) for about 15 minutes, or just until done.

notes: Can freeze dough logs for later use
Great appetizer crackers

recipes.title: Broccoli Stuffed Baked Vidalias
recipes.description: Vidalia onion halves stuffed with broccoli and topped with cream cheese sauce.

instructions.text: Peel and halve onions. Parboil in salted water 12 minutes; drain.
Meanwhile, microwave or briefly cook the broccoli and drain well.
Remove onion centers, leaving ¾-inch-thick shells.
Chop center portions to equal 1 cup.
Combine broccoli with chopped onions, Parmesan, mayo and lemon juice. Spoon into centers of onion halves.
For sauce, melt the butter in a small saucepan and blend in flour and salt.
Gradually whisk in milk and cook until thick, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and blend in cream cheese.
Spoon sauce over onion halves and bake, uncovered, at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes.

notes: From the Bland Farms Vidalia Onion Cookbook

recipes.title: Onion Squares
recipes.description: Savory biscuit-based squares topped with sautéed onions and sour cream.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Blend 1 egg and milk with biscuit mix and poppy seeds.
Turn dough into a greased 9-inch square baking pan.
Sauté onions in butter until tender.
Spread onions on dough.
Beat the other egg with sour cream and season with salt and pepper.
Spread sour cream mixture over onions.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes.
Cut into squares. Sprinkle with paprika.

notes: From Bland Farms, Glennville, GA - home of Vidalia onions

recipes.title: Libby's Outrageous Onion Cake
recipes.source_note: newspaper clipping (First place winner, onion festival)
recipes.description: Unexpected chocolate cake made with pureed Vidalia onion - first place winner at the onion festival!

instructions.text: Empty cake mix into the large bowl of an electric mixer. Add the eggs.
Puree the diced onion with the oil in a blender.
Add pureed onion mixture to the cake mix bowl and beat until a smooth cake batter forms.
Bake in two greased-and-floured 9-inch round cake pans at 325°F (165°C) for 25 minutes or until done.
Cool and split layers.
Fill with strawberry preserves.
Mix canned chocolate icing with powdered sugar, shortening (Crisco specified by Libby) and water.
Beat at high speed of an electric mixer until the frosting is light and fluffy.
Spread over the top and sides of cake.
Decorate as desired, choosing strawberry slices and/or chocolate shavings.

notes: First place winner at onion festival
Libby is a member of the onion-growing Bland family
The onion adds moisture - you can't taste it!

recipes.title: Orange-Flavored Beans with Tofu
recipes.description: Healthy Asian-inspired stir-fry with tofu, green beans, and orange sauce.

instructions.text: Prepare brown rice according to package directions; keep warm.
While rice is cooking, mix orange juice, red-pepper flakes, ginger, honey, soy sauce, garlic and rice vinegar in glass measuring cup.
Drain tofu; press gently with paper toweling to remove any excess moisture. Cut into ½-inch cubes.
Place tofu in 8x8-inch glass dish. Pour half of orange juice mixture over tofu; cover with plastic wrap; refrigerate to marinate for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring large pot of water to boiling. Add green and yellow beans; cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until crisp-tender. Drain.
Using knife, remove rind and bitter white pith from orange. Section, removing membranes and seeds. Cut sections into pieces.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat. Add beans and red pepper; sauté 5 minutes.
Add remaining orange juice mixture; cook another 3 minutes.
Remove tofu with slotted spoon from marinade and add to skillet; reserve marinade in dish. Stir orange pieces into skillet.
Whisk cornstarch into marinade in glass dish until smooth.
Stir into skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and clears, about 3 minutes.
Serve with brown rice. Sprinkle with green onion.

notes: FC Good Food - Pick of the Crop feature

recipes.title: Layered Eggplant
recipes.description: Fried eggplant slices layered with ricotta cheese mixture and topped with fresh tomato sauce.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Cut eggplant crosswise into 18 slices. Pat dry with paper toweling.
Mix together flour, salt and ¼ tsp pepper in shallow dish or onto waxed paper.
Heat ¼ cup oil in each of 2 large skillets over medium-high heat.
Dredge each eggplant slice in flour to coat both sides.
Fry 2 or 3 slices of eggplant per skillet until browned on both sides, about 4 minutes total. Transfer to paper toweling to drain. Repeat until all slices are fried, adding more oil as needed.
Mix cottage cheese or ricotta, Cheddar cheese, parsley, marjoram and remaining pepper in a bowl.

To assemble stacks: In large baking dish, place 1 slice eggplant. Spread on 3 tablespoons cottage cheese mixture; top with eggplant slice, 3 more tablespoons cottage cheese mixture and final slice of eggplant to make 6 stacks. Sprinkle with crumbs.
Bake, uncovered, in 400°F oven for 10 minutes.
Serve immediately with Fresh Tomato Sauce.

Fresh Tomato Sauce: Mix together in bowl 1 large tomato (seeded and diced), 3 tablespoons sliced fresh basil, 3 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, 3 tablespoons olive oil, ¼ tsp salt, and ⅛ tsp freshly ground black pepper. Makes about 1½ cups sauce.

notes: Fresh tomato sauce adds bright flavor

recipes.title: Karen Eatherly's Fruit and Cream Pie
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Graham cracker crust pie with cream cheese filling, whipped topping, and peach gelatin layer.

ingredients.item: fresh peach slices OR canned cling peaches

instructions.text: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Crust: Place graham crackers in plastic bag and seal. Using rolling pin, crush into fine crumbs; you should have about 1¼ cups crumbs.
Combine crumbs and sugar in bowl. Stir in melted butter.
Press over bottom and up sides of 9-inch pie pan.
Bake in 375°F oven for 6 to 9 minutes or until edges are brown. Cool on wire rack.
Filling: Beat together cream cheese and sugar in medium-size bowl until well mixed. Stir in whipped topping.
Spread mixture evenly into crust; refrigerate.
Stir together gelatin, pudding mix and water in medium-size saucepan.
Place over medium-low heat; stir constantly just until mixture comes to a boil.
Let cool 5 minutes.
Arrange fruit in attractive pattern over top of pie.
Spoon gelatin mixture over pie. Refrigerate 4 hours or until set.

notes: From FC Good Food Blue Ribbon Pies feature

recipes.title: Carol Thomas's Pecan Pie
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Classic Southern pecan pie with butterscotch chips.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Unfold piecrust; fit into 9-inch pie pan.
Scatter butterscotch chips and pecan pieces in pie shell.
Beat together butter, sugar, corn syrup and eggs in medium-size bowl.
Pour over nuts and butterscotch chips.
Bake in 350°F oven for 45 to 50 minutes or until golden brown.
If pie browns too quickly, cover with aluminum foil after 20 minutes.
Cool pie completely on wire rack.

notes: Butterscotch chips add extra flavor dimension
Cover with foil if browning too fast

recipes.title: Jo Beard's Chess Pie
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Classic Southern chess pie with cornmeal - a simple, custardy filling.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Unfold piecrust; fit into 9-inch pie pan.
Mix sugar and cornmeal in bowl.
Stir in butter, eggs, vinegar, salt and vanilla.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake in 350°F oven 45 minutes or until set.
If top starts to brown, lightly cover with foil about halfway through baking.
Cool pie completely on wire rack.

notes: Classic Southern dessert
Cornmeal gives it the traditional texture

recipes.title: Cathrine Brown's Cherry Pie
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (Family Circle, 9/1/98 - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Double-crust tart cherry pie with cinnamon.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Drain cherries, reserving 1 cup juice.
Mix ¼ cup sugar, cornstarch and cinnamon in saucepan.
Stir in cherry juice. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, 5 minutes, until smooth and thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir in cherries, remaining sugar, butter, and food coloring if desired.
Unfold 1 crust; fit into 9-inch pie pan. Pour in cherry mixture.
Unfold second crust; cover pie, in lattice pattern if desired. Crimp edges.
Bake in 425°F oven 45 minutes, until golden brown and bubbly.
If pie browns too quickly, cover edges with foil. Cool on wire rack.

notes: Food coloring is optional - enhances color

recipes.title: Kay McCrary's Fried Pies
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Old-fashioned fried hand pies with apricot filling.

instructions.text: Simmer apricots, peach and water in saucepan, uncovered, 12 to 15 minutes, until soft.
Put fruit with liquid and sugar in blender. Whirl until there are no lumps.
Mix flour and salt in large bowl. With pastry blender or 2 knives held like scissors, cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Add milk and blend in with fork until mixture comes together in a ball; add the extra milk if needed.
Roll dough out on lightly floured surface to ¼-inch thickness.
Use 3-inch round cookie cutter to cut out circles. Gather scraps together, roll out and cut into more circles.
Place about 2 teaspoons apricot mixture in center of each circle. Fold into half-moons; crimp edges.
Fry pies, no more than 5 at a time, in 375°F oil for 3 to 5 minutes or until golden.
Drain on paper towel-lined pan.

notes: Traditional Southern fried hand pies
Can use other dried fruits

recipes.title: Sheila Farris's Chocolate Pie
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Chocolate cream pie with meringue topping.

instructions.text: Unfold piecrust; fit into 9-inch pie pan. Prebake according to package directions. Remove from oven. Reduce temperature to 350°F (175°C).
Mix 1½ cups sugar, the flour and cocoa in medium-size heavy-bottomed saucepan. Stir in just enough milk to make paste; stir in remaining milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, 10 to 12 minutes or until thickened. Remove from heat.
Beat yolks in medium-size bowl until thick and yellow. Carefully whisk a little of hot cocoa mixture into yolks; whisk yolk mixture back into cocoa mixture.
Bring to boiling; remove from heat. Stir in vanilla and butter just until butter is melted. Pour into pie shell.
Beat egg whites in bowl just until frothy. Add cream of tartar and beat until peaks form.
Beat in the 6 tablespoons sugar, 2 tablespoons at a time, until stiff peaks form.
Spread meringue over pie filling so it touches all around the edge, sealing the top.
Bake in 350°F oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until meringue is lightly browned.
Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.

notes: Meringue must seal edges to prevent weeping

recipes.title: Corn Stew
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Pick of the Crop)
recipes.description: Creamy fresh corn stew with peppers and cheddar cheese.

ingredients.prep_note: shucked, kernels cut off cob (about 6 cups)

instructions.text: Melt butter in medium-size saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add onion; cook, stirring, until golden and glazed, about 5 minutes.
Add green and red peppers; cook, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add corn kernels.
Increase heat; cook, stirring, 2 minutes.
Add light cream, parsley, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Stir in 1 cup of Cheddar cheese and hot-pepper sauce until cheese has melted.
Ladle into bowls. Sprinkle with remaining ¼ cup shredded cheese. Serve warm.

notes: Best with fresh corn in season

recipes.title: Beet Summer Salad
recipes.description: Warm beet and cucumber salad with honey-herb dressing and hard-cooked eggs.

instructions.text: Bring 2 quarts of water in saucepan to boiling. Add ½ tsp salt and 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Add beets; cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes. Drain; reserve broth for beet soup if desired.
Meanwhile, combine remaining salt and lemon juice, the honey and wine vinegar in large bowl; remove half of the mixture and reserve for dressing for greens.
Cut cucumbers into slices. Add to honey mixture in bowl; let stand to marinate.
When beets are cool enough to handle but still warm, remove skins. Slice in half; cut crosswise into ¼-inch-thick slices; place in bowl. Set aside, covered.
Remove cucumbers with slotted spoon from marinade and place in small saucepan. Add chicken broth; gently cook until liquid evaporates, 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Mix beets, parsley, dill and thyme in bowl.
Whisk oil into reserved honey mixture along with any marinade left over from cucumbers. Add greens; toss to coat.
Divide greens equally among 6 plates. Arrange beets, cucumbers and egg wedges on plates.
Serve warm or at room temperature with sour cream.

notes: Save beet cooking liquid for soup

recipes.title: Garlicky Broccoli Rabe
recipes.description: Fettuccine with broccoli rabe in a creamy garlic sauce with two cheeses.

instructions.text: Bring large pot of salted water to boiling.
Simmer garlic, cream, broth and pepper flakes in small saucepan 20 minutes, until garlic is softened. Mash garlic into cream to blend.
Add pasta to boiling water; cook following package directions.
Heat oil in large skillet. Add broccoli rabe; sauté 3 minutes.
Add ¼ cup water; cook until water evaporates, about 5 minutes. Add salt and pepper. Remove from heat.
Drain pasta; return to pot.
Add rabe; spoon garlic mixture over top.
Sprinkle with Parmesan and Fontina cheeses; toss to mix.

notes: Note: Broccoli can be used in place of broccoli rabe. Cut flowerets from 2 pounds broccoli; cut stem in 1-inch pieces. Add to pasta in pot during last 5 minutes of cooking.
Serve with lemon wedges.
Drain and plunge into ice water to stop cooking and preserve bright green color.

recipes.title: Rachel Gregory's Apple Pie
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Classic lattice-top apple pie with orange juice and apple pie spice.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Unfold 1 crust; fit into 9-inch pie pan.
Mix sugar and flour in bowl.
Cook apples and juice in saucepan for 5 to 6 minutes, until apples are tender.
Pour into pie. Sprinkle with sugar mixture. Dot with butter.
Unfold second crust; make lattice top. Sprinkle with pie spice.
Bake in 375°F oven 45 minutes or until golden brown and bubbly.
Cool on wire rack.

notes: Orange juice adds a subtle citrus flavor

recipes.title: Sammie Major's Fudge Pie
recipes.source_note: magazine clipping (FC Good Food - Blue Ribbon Pies)
recipes.description: Rich chocolate fudge pie in a prebaked shell.

instructions.text: Unfold piecrust; fit into 9-inch pie pan. Prebake crust according to package directions. Remove from oven.
Lower the oven temperature to 325°F (165°C).
Beat together sugar, flour, cocoa powder, butter, eggs and vanilla in medium-size bowl.
Spoon into pie shell.
Bake in 325°F oven 25 to 30 minutes or until set.
Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.

notes: Simple but intensely chocolatey

recipes.title: Julia's Pastry
recipes.description: Sour cream pastry crust recipe.

instructions.text: Cut butter into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Mix in sour cream and water until dough comes together.
Chill before rolling out.

notes: Also contains prep notes: chop garlic saute slowly, dice tomatoes, dice chicken, chop basil, cook pasta

recipes.title: Squash Casserole
recipes.description: Southern squash casserole topped with crumbled cornbread.

instructions.text: Sauté onions in butter until soft.
Add cut up squash and cook until tender (reserve cooking liquid).
Add package of cheese to the hot squash mixture.
Crumble baked cornbread over the mixture.
Add some cooking liquid to moisten.
Transfer to casserole dish.
Bake covered for 1 hour, uncovering the last 30 minutes to brown the top.

notes: Traditional Southern side dish
Temperature inferred - standard casserole temp

recipes.title: Sangria
recipes.description: Homemade Spanish-style sangria with orange liqueur and brandy.

instructions.text: Combine liqueur, brandy and sugar.
When sugar has dissolved, add wine and club soda.
If desired, add slices of fruit.
Store in refrigerator in tightly closed bottle.

notes: Donna advises: buy a large bottle of wine for better price per ounce
Add fresh bottle of club soda each time you serve, as it goes flat after opening

recipes.title: Hooters Buffalo Chicken Wings
recipes.description: Nearly world famous. Often imitated, hardly ever duplicated. Copycat recipe for Hooters-style buffalo wings.

ingredients.item: Crystal Louisiana Hot Sauce or Frank's Red Hot Cayenne Sauce

instructions.text: Heat oil in a deep fryer to 375°F. You want just enough oil to cover the wings entirely—an inch or so deep at least.
Combine the butter, hot sauce, ground pepper, and garlic powder in a small saucepan over low heat. Heat until the butter is melted and the ingredients are well-blended.
Combine the flour, paprika, cayenne pepper, and salt in a small bowl.
If the wings are frozen, be sure to defrost and dry them. Put the wings into a large bowl and sprinkle the flour mixture over them, coating each wing evenly.
Put the wings in the refrigerator for 60 to 90 minutes. (This will help the breading to stick to the wings when fried.)
Put all the wings into the hot oil and fry them for 10 to 15 minutes or until some parts of the wings begin to turn dark brown.
Remove the wings from the oil to a paper towel to drain. But don't let them sit too long, because you want to serve the wings hot.

Quickly put the wings into a large bowl. Add the hot sauce and stir, coating all of the wings evenly. You could also use a large plastic container (such as Tupperware) with a lid for this. Put all the wings inside the container, add the sauce, put on the lid, then shake.
Serve with bleu cheese dressing and celery sticks on the side.

notes: From Top Secret Recipes cookbook
Hooters started in Clearwater, Florida on April Fool's Day 1983
The refrigeration step is key for crispy coating

recipes.title: Carrot Raisin Muffins
recipes.description: Wholesome muffins with carrots, pineapple, and raisins.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease or line 12 muffin cups.
Mix dry ingredients (flours, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger) in a large bowl.
In another bowl, combine beaten eggs, crushed pineapple (with juice), grated carrot, raisins, corn syrup, and vanilla.
Add wet ingredients to dry and stir just until combined.
Fold in nuts if using.
Fill muffin cups ⅔ full.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20 minutes or until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

notes: The pineapple keeps these moist

recipes.title: Amaranth (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: The sacred grain of the Aztecs, domesticated in Mexico 7,000 years ago. Can be cooked as porridge or toasted.

instructions.text: Use a ratio of 3 cups liquid to 1 cup amaranth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes.
If necessary, remove from heat and let sit, covered, until liquid is absorbed. Do not allow to boil over, because it is very sticky.
Do not salt until thoroughly cooked.
Alternatively, toast 1 cup of seeds in skillet or saucepan for 2 to 4 minutes or until the seeds pop.
Bring 1 cup water plus 1 tsp vegetable oil to a boil, add toasted amaranth, and simmer for 7 minutes or until liquid has been absorbed.
Remove from heat and let steam for an additional 5 to 10 minutes.
Stir in raisins, chopped dates or nuts, honey, molasses or maple syrup for breakfast cereal. Mix with corn, green onions and cooked pinto beans for an entree or side dish.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains For Robust Flavors' feature

recipes.title: Barley (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: Possibly the oldest grain on the planet, barley can grow in virtually any climate.

instructions.text: Combine 3½ to 4 cups stock with 1 cup barley, plus salt and butter to taste.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, until liquid is absorbed and barley is tender.
Serve with butter or use as an ingredient in recipes.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains For Robust Flavors' feature

recipes.title: Oat Groats (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: The whole grain with only the inedible chaff removed. Chewy texture and almost-meaty flavor.

instructions.text: Toast 1 cup oats in saucepan or skillet over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, until aromatic and slightly darker, about 4 minutes.
Boil 1¾ cups water or stock with salt and butter to taste, add the oats, simmer covered for 45 minutes until liquid absorbed.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 10 minutes, then fluff.
Serve with butter or toasted nuts.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains' feature

recipes.title: Polenta (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: A staple in many regions of Italy, made of meal ground from flint corn.

instructions.text: For every 1 cup polenta, bring 3 cups salted water to boil.
Slowly whisk in polenta, then reduce heat to medium.
Stir with wooden spoon, stirring frequently, about 30 minutes until thick and pulls from sides.
Stir in 1 tbsp olive oil, scrape into bowl, rest 7 minutes before turning out.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains' feature

recipes.title: Quinoa (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: Cultivated in the Andes 8,000 years ago. Very high in protein, expands 4x when cooked.

instructions.text: Rinse several times before cooking to remove bitterness.
Bring 2 cups water to boil for every 1 cup quinoa.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Use as stuffing for vegetables, with salsas or chutneys, or with fruits and nuts.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains' feature
Rinse before cooking to remove bitter coating

recipes.title: Hard Red Winter Wheat Berries (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: Wheat is the world's most widely distributed grain, grown in virtually every country.

instructions.text: Bring 3 cups water to boil, add 1 cup wheat berries, reduce heat and simmer for 1½ hours.
Do not add salt.
Serve as side dish with butter, salt, pepper and parsley, or use for grain salad with bean sprouts, carrots and green onions.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains' feature

recipes.title: Kamut (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: Ancient grain dating to 6,000 years ago in Egypt. Chewy texture and mildly nutty taste.

instructions.text: Combine 1 cup kamut with 2 cups lightly salted water.
Bring to boil, reduce heat and simmer until tender, about 50 minutes to 1 hour.
Kamut triples in volume when cooked.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains' feature

recipes.title: Millet (Cooking Guide)
recipes.description: Ancient grain brought to the American heartland by Russian Mennonites in the 19th century.

instructions.text: Use ratio of 3 cups liquid to 1 cup millet.
Bring to boil, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes.
Remove from heat, fluff and let sit covered for 10 minutes.
Use as base for sauteed vegetables.

notes: Part of 'Go With The Grains' feature

recipes.title: Roasted Veggie Tacos
recipes.description: Vegetarian tacos with roasted peppers, tomatoes, and onions served with refried beans.

instructions.text: Place 1 oven rack in bottom rack position. Heat oven to 475°F (245°C).
Spread tomatoes, bell peppers and onions in ungreased 15-by-10-inch baking pan. Drizzle with oil; toss to coat.
Sprinkle with taco seasoning; toss to evenly coat.
Bake at 475°F on bottom oven rack for 15 minutes or until bell peppers and onions are crisp-tender.
Meanwhile, spread 2 tbsp refried beans on half of inside of each taco shell. Arrange taco shells on ungreased cookie sheet.
Place tacos on middle oven rack with vegetables. Bake 1 to 2 minutes more until tacos are warmed.
To serve, spoon about ⅓ cup vegetable mixture over refried bean in each shell. Serve with salsa.

recipes.title: Butterscotch Schnapps Cookies
recipes.attribution: Carol Drake, St. Clair Shores, MI
recipes.description: Soft cookies made with yellow cake mix and butterscotch chips, finished with butterscotch schnapps drizzle.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease cookie sheets.
Cream butter and cream cheese. Blend in egg and vanilla.
Mix in cake mix by hand. Mix in butterscotch chips.
Drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet.
Bake 8-10 minutes. Remove from oven and let cool on cookie sheet.
Lace each cookie with Butterscotch Schnapps, a couple of drops, using a teaspoon.

notes: You may substitute chocolate chips and Peppermint Schnapps for a variation

recipes.title: Ring in the New Year Soup
recipes.description: Traditional Southern black-eye pea soup for New Year's Day good luck, with sausage and rice.

instructions.text: Combine black-eye peas, water, tomatoes, rice and salt in crockpot or soup pot.
Brown sausage, onion and bell pepper, drain and add to black-eye pea mixture.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
When ready to serve, top with sour cream and shredded cheddar cheese.

notes: Southern New Year's tradition - black-eye peas bring good luck!
Can be made in crockpot or on stovetop

recipes.title: Coconut Delights
recipes.description: No-bake coconut date balls rolled in graham cracker crumbs.

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients together.
Chill mixture for ½ hour.
Shape into balls and roll in graham crackers.

notes: No-bake recipe

recipes.title: Grandma's Peanut Butter Cookies
recipes.description: Classic peanut butter cookies with the signature criss-cross fork pattern.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl, cream shortening, peanut butter and sugars.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour, baking soda and salt; gradually add to creamed mixture.
Roll into 1-1/2-inch balls and place 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets.
Flatten with a fork, pressing once in each direction to make criss-cross pattern.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 10-15 minutes or until bottoms are lightly browned.
Remove to wire racks to cool.

notes: Use shiny aluminum baking sheets without sides for golden brown cookies
Preheat oven 10-15 minutes before baking

recipes.title: Virginia's Pickled Veggies
recipes.description: Quick pickling brine for mixed vegetables - cucumbers, beans, squash, carrots.

instructions.text: Combine sugar, white vinegar, water, salt and dill in a pot.
Boil for 1 minute.
Pour over veggies - unpeeled cucumbers, beans, sliced squash, carrots, etc.
Add clove of garlic to each jar.

notes: Amount of sugar can be reduced to 1½ cups

recipes.title: Pickled Beans (Dilly Beans)
recipes.description: Classic dilly beans for canning - crisp pickled green beans with garlic and dill.

ingredients.prep_note: chopped, or sprig fresh dill per jar

instructions.text: Snip beans and parboil unsalted for 10 minutes. Cool in ice water.
Place clove garlic in each jar. Add 2 tbsp chopped dill, or sprig of fresh dill.
Heat 2 cups water, 2 cups white vinegar, 4 tsp sugar, and 4 tbsp salt.
Bring to boil and pour over beans in jar to full. Seal.

notes: Parboiling and ice bath keeps beans crisp
For proper canning, follow current USDA guidelines

recipes.title: Oatmeal Cookies
recipes.description: Classic oatmeal cookies with raisins and nuts.

instructions.text: Cream sugar and oleo together.
Add eggs and mix well.
Combine flour, oatmeal, baking soda, baking powder, and cinnamon.
Add dry ingredients alternately with milk.
Stir in raisins and nuts.
Drop by spoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake until golden brown.

notes: Oleo is margarine - can substitute butter

recipes.title: Old Fashioned Spare Ribs
recipes.description: Tender spare ribs slow-cooked in a tangy tomato-based sauce.

instructions.text: Put ribs in roaster.
Stir up the sauce: combine catsup, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, chili powder, water, and chopped onion.
Pour sauce over meat.
Cook covered about 2 hours at 350°F (175°C).
Uncover for 30 minutes.
Turn and baste several times during cooking.

notes: Baste several times for best results

recipes.title: Rhubarb Pie (Handwritten)
recipes.description: Classic rhubarb pie with egg-enriched filling.

instructions.text: Mix rhubarb, flour, sugar, beaten egg, and salt together.
Pour into unbaked pie crust.
Dot with butter.
Add top crust if desired.
Bake at 450°F (230°C) for 45 minutes.

notes: High temperature - watch carefully

recipes.title: Lois' Ice Box Pickles
recipes.description: Refrigerator pickles with turmeric and pickling spices - no canning required.

instructions.text: Heat sugar and vinegar to dissolve the sugar.
Add salt, turmeric, celery seed, and mustard seed.
Pour over prepared cucumbers in jars.
Refrigerate - no canning needed.

notes: Ice box pickles store in refrigerator, not shelf-stable

recipes.title: Bread & Butter Pickles
recipes.description: Classic sweet bread and butter pickles with pickling spices.

instructions.text: Slice cucumbers and onions, layer with salt, let sit, then drain.
Heat vinegar and sugar with mustard seed, celery seed, and turmeric.
Add drained cucumbers and onions.
Pack into jars and process according to canning guidelines.

notes: Classic sweet pickle recipe
Follow USDA canning guidelines for safe processing

recipes.title: Janet's Pie
recipes.description: No-bake peanut butter cream cheese pie with Cool Whip topping.

instructions.text: Beat cream cheese, sugar, and peanut butter together until smooth.
Add 8 oz (or ½ container) of Cool Whip and mix well.
Pour into prepared pie crust.
Spread remaining Cool Whip on top.
Refrigerate until set.

notes: No-bake recipe
Can use sugar substitute for diabetic-friendly version

recipes.title: Erdine's Rice Crispies
recipes.description: Peanut butter Rice Krispies treats topped with chocolate and butterscotch chips.

instructions.text: Heat sugar and corn syrup to boiling.
Add peanut butter and mix together well.
Add Rice Krispies and stir to coat.
Press into 9x13 pan.
Top with ½ package chocolate chips and ½ package butterscotch chips while still warm.
Let chips melt, then spread evenly. Let cool and cut into bars.

notes: No-bake recipe
Spread chips while treats are warm to melt

recipes.title: Corn Pudding
recipes.description: Fresh corn pudding with ham, eggs, and Parmesan cheese.

instructions.text: Cut corn off 4 ears of corn.
Saute corn in olive oil. Add onions, ham, salt and pepper.
Whisk 6 eggs with 1 cup milk.
Add egg mixture to corn mixture.
Add nutmeg and Parmesan cheese.
Pour into baking dish and bake at 325°F (165°C) for 45 minutes to 1 hour until set.

notes: Great way to use fresh summer corn

missing_inputs: exact amounts for onions, ham, cheese

recipes.title: Oven Potatoes
recipes.description: Crispy oven-baked potato wedges coated in flour and Parmesan cheese.

instructions.text: Mix flour and Parmesan cheese together.
Cut potatoes into wedges and coat in flour-cheese mixture.
Place on cookie sheet.
Drizzle melted oleo (or butter) over top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until done, about 45 minutes.

notes: Simple and delicious side dish

recipes.title: Baked Chicken (Pepsi Can)
recipes.description: Beer-can style chicken using Pepsi for moist, flavorful roasted chicken.

instructions.text: Open a can of Pepsi and pour out (or drink) half.
Add lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce to the can.
Set chicken over the can so it stands upright.
Bake until chicken is cooked through and golden.

notes: Similar to beer can chicken - the soda keeps the chicken moist

recipes.title: Texas Squealer
recipes.description: Quick sausage and pepper wrap with hot salsa.

instructions.text: Cook sausage with onion and pepper.
Place mixture on tortilla shell.
Add hot salsa.
Roll up and eat!

notes: Quick and easy meal

recipes.title: Orange Chocolate Biscotti with Almonds
recipes.description: Chocolate biscotti made easy with cake mix, flavored with orange zest and studded with almonds.

instructions.text: Mix cake mix, melted butter, eggs, flour, almonds, and orange zest in large mixing bowl.
Blend with mixer until well mixed - dough will be thick and form a large ball.
Pat ball on greased cookie sheet. Flour hands and shape into a log about 14x4x½ inches, a little higher in center.
Bake biscotti until toothpick comes out clean, 30-35 minutes.
Remove from oven (leave oven on) and let cool for 10 minutes.
Cutting on baking sheet with serrated knife, slice into ¾-inch slices.
Lay slices on their side on baking sheet.
Return to oven and bake 10 minutes.
Turn oven off and leave biscotti in oven for 30 minutes.
Cool 2 hours. Store in airtight container.

notes: Uses cake mix for easy preparation
Perfect for dipping in coffee

recipes.title: Tempura Batter (for Chicken)
recipes.description: Light, crispy tempura batter for fried chicken.

instructions.text: Mix flour, club soda, egg, and buttermilk to form batter.
Dip chicken pieces in batter.
Fry to golden brown.
Put in oven to finish cooking if needed.

notes: Club soda makes the batter extra light and crispy

recipes.title: Pickled Beans (Variant)
recipes.description: Another version of dilly beans for canning.

instructions.text: Snip beans and parboil for 10 minutes.
Cool in ice water.
Put ½ clove garlic in each jar.
Add 2 tbsp chopped dill or sprig to each jar.
Heat water, vinegar, sugar, and salt - bring to boil.
Pour over beans and seal.

recipes.title: Pickled Veggies (Variant)
recipes.description: Simple pickling brine for vegetables.

instructions.text: Combine sugar, water, vinegar, and salt.
Boil for 1 minute.
Pour over prepared vegetables.

notes: Sugar amount can be adjusted to taste

recipes.title: Blueberry Muffins
recipes.description: Classic homemade blueberry muffins.

instructions.text: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt together (dry ingredients).
In separate bowl, mix egg, oil, and milk.
Pour wet ingredients over dry ingredients.
Fold in blueberries.
Fill muffin cups about ⅔ full.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes.

recipes.variant_notes: Files 660 and 1080 show same recipe with slight variation: 1/3 cup oil (vs 1/2 cup), 1 cup blueberries (vs 1.25 cups)

recipes.title: Heath Bars (Saltine Toffee)
recipes.description: Addictive saltine cracker toffee topped with chocolate - also known as Christmas Crack!

instructions.text: Line cookie sheet with foil.
Lay crackers in single layer on foil.
Melt butter and brown sugar over medium heat.
Bring to boil for 3 minutes, stirring constantly!
Cool 2 minutes, then pour over crackers.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 5 minutes.
Pour chocolate chips on top and smooth over as chocolate melts.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts if desired.
Let cool completely, then break into pieces.

notes: Also called Christmas Crack or Cracker Candy
Marked 'good' in original recipe!

recipes.title: Janet's Salad (Ramen Noodle Salad)
recipes.description: Crunchy Asian-style cabbage salad with toasted ramen noodles and almonds.

instructions.text: Chop cabbage and onion.
Brown broken ramen noodles and almonds in a pan. Add sesame seeds.
Make dressing: combine sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and seasoning packet from ramen noodles.
Toss cabbage and onion with dressing.
Top with toasted noodles, almonds, and sesame seeds just before serving.

notes: Add crunchy toppings just before serving to maintain crunch

recipes.title: Lena's Cream Pie
recipes.description: Simple no-bake cream cheese pie with optional berries.

instructions.text: Beat cream cheese and sugar together until smooth.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Refrigerate until set.
Top with fresh berries if desired.

notes: No-bake recipe
Great with strawberries or blueberries

recipes.title: Fran's Dump Cake
recipes.description: Grandma Baker's easy dump cake with pineapple and fruit pie filling topped with yellow cake mix.

instructions.text: Spread chopped pecans on bottom of 9x13 pan.
Spread crushed pineapple over pecans.
Spread fruit pie filling over pineapple.
Sprinkle dry yellow cake mix evenly over top.
Drizzle melted butter over cake mix.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) until golden and bubbly.

notes: Called 'dump cake' because you just dump in the ingredients
No mixing required!

recipes.title: Broccoli Salad with Bacon and Eggs
recipes.description: Creamy broccoli salad with mashed hard-boiled eggs and crispy bacon.

instructions.text: Cut up broccoli into bite-size florets.
Add chopped onion.
Add mashed hard-boiled eggs.
Add crushed crispy bacon.
Mix dressing: mayo, vinegar (or lemon juice), a little sugar, salt and pepper.
Toss salad with dressing.

notes: Best when chilled for a few hours before serving

recipes.title: Constipation Recipe (Prune-Fig Remedy)
recipes.description: Traditional home remedy with prunes, figs, raisins, and senna tea.

instructions.text: Steep 4 oz senna tea in 1 pint of boiling water for 20 minutes.
Strain the tea.
Cook prunes, figs, raisins, lemon juice, and brown sugar with the strained tea for 5 minutes.
Store in refrigerator or freezer.
Take 2 tablespoons at breakfast.

notes: Can be frozen
Can make ½ batch
Traditional home remedy - consult doctor before use

recipes.title: Ethel's Pie Crust
recipes.description: Reliable pie crust recipe using Crisco, makes multiple crusts.

ingredients.prep_note: enough to make 1 cup with egg

instructions.text: Mix flour, salt, and baking powder.
Cut in Crisco until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Beat egg in a 1-cup measure, add water to make 1 cup total.
Add vinegar to egg mixture.
Add wet ingredients to flour mixture and mix until dough forms.
Divide into portions and roll out as needed.

notes: Use 4 cups flour if using lard instead of Crisco
Vinegar makes crust tender

recipes.title: Raisin Scones
recipes.description: Classic British-style raisin scones with nutrition information.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Whisk milk and egg together.
Mix dry ingredients in another bowl.
Drop the butter into the flour and using your fingers, rub until the mixture is pebbly.
Pour in milk and egg mixture. Mix with a fork until dough is evenly moist.
Add raisins and stir.
Spoon a dozen mounds of dough onto baking sheet.
Bake for 20-22 minutes until golden.

recipes.title: Rhubarb Cake (with Jello and Marshmallows)
recipes.description: Rhubarb dessert layered with Jello and marshmallows, topped with yellow cake.

instructions.text: Put chopped rhubarb in 9x14 inch pan.
Sprinkle sugar over rhubarb.
Sprinkle dry Jello powder over sugar.
Layer mini marshmallows on top.
Prepare yellow cake mix according to package directions.
Pour prepared cake batter on top of marshmallows.
Bake at 325°F (165°C) for about 1 hour.

notes: The marshmallows create a gooey layer
Rhubarb sinks to bottom during baking

recipes.title: Dump Cake - Jean B
recipes.description: Easy dump cake with pineapple, cherry pie filling, and coconut topped with cake mix and butter.

instructions.text: Lightly grease a 9x13 inch pan.
Dump in crushed pineapple and spread evenly.
Spoon cherry pie filling over the pineapple.
Dump in flaked coconut as evenly as you can.
Dump box of yellow cake mix over all.
Pour melted butter over top of cake.
Sprinkle top with chopped nuts.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) until brown on top, about 45 minutes.

notes: Great eaten warm or with Cool Whip
Variant technique: Mix cake mix with melted butter before spreading over fruit. Use pastry blender to mix.
recipes.variant_notes: This version adds coconut and uses butter instead of margarine

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cookies (Flourless)
recipes.source_note: Newspaper clipping - recipe shared for Jewel Curley of Largo
recipes.description: Simple 4-ingredient flourless peanut butter cookies - naturally gluten-free.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix together all ingredients until well combined.
Roll into balls using about 1 teaspoon of dough for each.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Press tops with fork to create criss-cross pattern.
Bake at 350°F for 12 minutes or until lightly browned.

notes: This is the famous 4-ingredient flourless peanut butter cookie recipe
Naturally gluten-free

recipes.title: Classic Lasagna (Johnsonville)
recipes.description: Hearty layered lasagna with Italian sausage, ricotta, and mozzarella using no-boil noodles.

ingredients.item: Barilla Italian Baking Sauce or Marinara

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Spray baking pan (13x9x3 inch deep) with nonstick cooking spray.
Remove 16 lasagna noodles from box. DO NOT BOIL.
In medium bowl, beat eggs. Stir in ricotta, 2 cups mozzarella and Parmesan.
Layer lasagna, slightly overlapping sheets. Lasagna will expand to edges during cooking. Spread fillings to edges to seal in and cook lasagna during baking.
Layer in following order: 1 cup sauce on bottom, 4 uncooked noodles, 1/3 ricotta mixture, half of browned meat, 1 cup mozzarella, 1 cup sauce.
Layer 4 uncooked noodles, 1/3 ricotta mixture, and 1.5 cups sauce.
Layer 4 uncooked noodles, remaining ricotta mixture, browned meat, and 1 cup sauce.
Layer 4 uncooked noodles and remaining sauce.
Bake covered with foil until bubbly, 50-60 minutes.
Uncover. Add remaining 1 cup mozzarella and continue cooking until cheese is melted, about 5 minutes.
Let stand 15 minutes before cutting.

notes: If using a 2-inch deep pan, make 3 layers to avoid possible boiling over. Use same amount of filling and 12 uncooked noodles.

recipes.title: Gingerbread House
recipes.source_note: The Tampa Tribune, 1996 - from 'An Edible Christmas' by Irena Chalmers (Morrow)
recipes.description: Complete gingerbread house with dough recipe and detailed assembly instructions using royal icing and candy decorations.

instructions.text: DOUGH: In a medium bowl, sift flour, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl with electric mixer at high, beat shortening and sugar 3 minutes. Add molasses and egg; beat 3 minutes or until well blended.
Add flour mixture and stir, by hand, to form smooth dough. Divide dough in half, wrap each half in plastic, and refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Make 3 patterns for the house: one side, one end, and one roof pattern.
Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly dust flour on ungreased cookie sheet or back of ungreased jelly-roll pan.
Roll one ball of dough to 1/8-inch thick. Lay out cardboard patterns and cut around each one with knife. Remove excess dough.
Run knife around each piece to clean up ragged edges. Bake 15 to 18 minutes.
Immediately run a long spatula under each piece to prevent sticking. Let cool 5 minutes on cookie sheet; transfer to wire rack; cool completely.

ICING: In a large bowl, stir confectioners' sugar and egg whites. With electric mixer, beat at high 5 minutes until mixture is stiff. Fill a zipper bag with icing, seal, and snip one corner to make a 1/4-inch hole.
TO ASSEMBLE: Decorate front end piece and two side pieces as desired, using icing as glue.

Pipe thick line of icing along bottom edge of back end piece; pipe thick line of icing on bottom and back edges of one side piece. Stand and join the back end and side on cardboard base, holding in place several minutes. Use tall glasses to support while drying.
Reinforce house with icing along inside joints. Add remaining side and front pieces the same way. Let set.
TO ADD ROOF: Pipe icing along top edges; press roof pieces into place and hold for several minutes. Let icing set completely.
FOR THATCH ROOF: Split shredded-wheat biscuits in half lengthwise. Pipe two thick rows of icing on inside of each half; press halves onto roof to create 'thatch' rows. Cover both sides.
Decorate front edge of roof with thick line of icing studded with jelly beans.
Make 'icicles' on bottom edges of roof by piping large dots of icing and pulling pastry tip downward.
Make chimney on back end of roof from jelly beans stacked like bricks.

notes: Makes 6 pieces for the house: 1 front end, 1 back end, 2 sides, 2 roof pieces
Royal icing sets hard - work quickly

recipes.title: Min's Cake
recipes.description: Simple yellow cake with vanilla - a basic homestyle recipe.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix oleo, sugar, and vanilla together.
Crack 2 eggs into a measuring cup and fill the rest with milk. Beat well.
Add egg-milk mixture to the oleo mixture and beat well.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt. Add to wet ingredients.
Pour into greased pan and bake at 350°F until done.

notes: Faded/stained card - some details difficult to read
The eggs-in-cup-filled-with-milk technique was common in older recipes

flags: Card stained and faded, some measurements approximate

recipes.title: Cherry Fruitcake
recipes.description: Rich fruitcake with raisins, candied cherries, citron, and rum - makes a 5-pound cake.

instructions.text: In bowl, combine raisins, cherries, citron, and rum; with spoon, mix well.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C). Grease 10-inch tube pan. Line bottom and side with brown paper.
In large bowl of mixer, at medium speed, beat butter with sugar and extract until fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
At low speed, gradually beat in flour.
Add prepared raisin mixture. Turn out into prepared pan.
Bake about 2 hours and 25 minutes, or until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean.
Let cool in pan on wire rack 30 minutes. Turn out of pan; let cool completely on rack.

notes: Line pan with brown paper for easy removal
Low temperature and long baking time prevents burning

recipes.title: Evelyn J. Wilson's Fruitcake
recipes.description: A lavish fruitcake loaded with dried fruits, nuts, and soaked in rum and orange liqueur.

ingredients.prep_note: can substitute pineapple or orange juice

instructions.text: Have all ingredients at room temperature. Mix first seven ingredients (fruits and nuts) in a large bowl; add 1 cup of the flour and mix with wooden spoon to coat mixture.
Sift remaining 2 cups of flour once, then add mace, salt and spices. Sift again.
Cream butter in electric mixer; add both sugars gradually, creaming well.
Stir in the 4 beaten eggs and beat until smooth and fluffy; stir in molasses and extracts.
Add remaining flour gradually and alternately with sherry and grape juice.
Pour batter into fruit and nut mixture. Mix with hands or wooden spoon, lifting fruit and nuts through mixture until well distributed.
Take the egg whites and mix well with wooden spoon through mixture.
Place in foil loaf pans (3 to 4 pans). Do not fill to top.
Bake at 350°F (175°C), 2 to 2½ hours, or until cakes test done.
Cool cakes in pan; remove and seal with foil or plastic wrap. Store in sealed containers.
Open seal and add rum; seal. A few days later, open seal and add orange liqueur.

notes: Age cake with rum and orange liqueur for best flavor
Non-alcoholic version: use extra fruit juice instead of sherry

recipes.title: Rice Krispie Dessert
recipes.description: Frozen dessert with a crispy Rice Krispie crust layered with ice cream.

instructions.text: Combine Rice Krispies, melted butter, coconut, chopped nuts, and brown sugar.
Spread half of mixture in an 8-inch pan.
Cover with 1 pint ice cream.
Spread on remaining mixture.
Return to freezer until ready to serve.
Remove a few minutes before ready to serve. Cut and serve.

notes: Use any flavor ice cream you prefer

recipes.title: Bacon Bites
recipes.description: Sweet and savory candied bacon bites cooked in the microwave - addictive party appetizer.

instructions.text: Arrange bacon slices, about 6 at a time, in a single layer on a microwave roasting rack set in a glass baking dish.
Combine brown sugar and mustard.
Sprinkle evenly over bacon.
Cook on high 1 minute per bacon slice.
Drain on paper towels.
Break into bite-sized pieces when cool.

recipes.pan_size: Microwave roasting rack in glass dish
notes: Also known as 'Millionaire Bacon' or 'Pig Candy'
Can also be baked in oven at 400°F

recipes.title: Oatmeal Cake
recipes.description: Moist oatmeal cake with brown sugar and cinnamon.

instructions.text: In a medium bowl, pour water on oats, set aside and let stand 20 minutes.
In a large bowl, cream shortening, sugars, eggs, salt, and cinnamon.
Add oat mixture, stir well.
Add flour and soda, mix again.
Pour into a greased 9-by-13-inch pan.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30-40 minutes.
A few minutes before cake is done, make topping.

notes: Original recipe mentions 'Cake Topping (below)' but topping recipe was cut off
Typically topped with broiled coconut-pecan frosting

flags: Topping recipe cut off from clipping

recipes.title: Graham Cracker Village
recipes.description: Holiday craft project - miniature houses and churches made from milk cartons and graham crackers decorated with frosting.
recipes.servings_yield: 4 houses or 1 church and 1 tree (per can of frosting)

ingredients.prep_note: 2½-by-2½-inch squares, 8 for each house, 18 for each church

instructions.text: Cut upright center seal from milk carton; securely tape center together to form roof.
Completely cover 2 sides of carton with ¼-inch thick layer of frosting.
Firmly press 1 graham cracker square on each frosted side of carton. Repeat for remaining sides.
Fill in front and back peaks with frosting. If desired, cut crackers to fit peaks; press in place.
Cover roof portion with ¼-inch layer of frosting.
Cut 3 crackers in half, forming 6 rectangles. Arrange 3 halves vertically on each side of roof; press in place. (There will be some overhang.)
Allow frosting to set about 10 minutes.
Place frosting in decorating bag with star or open tip. Decorate houses with frosting and candies, using frosting to secure candies.
Repeat to make each house.

notes: If 8-ounce milk cartons are not available, quart cartons can be used - cut 5 inches off bottom of each carton
One can of frosting will frost 4 houses or 1 church and 1 tree
Great holiday project for kids

recipes.title: Easy Pesto Pinwheels
recipes.description: Quick and easy appetizers made with crescent rolls, pesto, and roasted red peppers.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Unroll dough into two long rectangles. Firmly press perforations to smooth.
Spread rectangles with pesto to within ¼-inch of edges; sprinkle with bell peppers.
Starting at shortest side, roll up each rectangle; pinch edges to seal.
Cut each roll into eight slices.
Place, cut side down, on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350°F for 13 to 17 minutes or until golden brown.
Immediately remove from cookie sheet. Serve warm.

notes: Can substitute sun-dried tomatoes for roasted peppers
Make ahead and refrigerate before baking

recipes.title: White Chocolate Snack Mix
recipes.description: Sweet and salty snack mix coated in white chocolate.

instructions.text: [UNCLEAR - instructions not visible on card. Likely: Melt white chocolate and coat cereal mixture, then spread to cool.]

notes: Instructions not visible on card - typical method is to melt white chocolate, mix with dry ingredients, spread on waxed paper to set

flags: Instructions not visible on original card

recipes.title: No-Stir Polenta
recipes.description: Easy oven-baked polenta that requires no stirring - adjust water for desired consistency.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a heavy, ovenproof, 12-inch saucepan.
Add polenta, water, butter and salt to pan. Stir with a fork until blended. (It will separate and won't come together until more than half of the cooking time has elapsed.)
Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Stir the polenta with a long-pronged fork, add salt to taste, and bake 10 minutes longer.
Remove from the oven; let rest for 5 minutes before pouring into a buttered bowl.
Serve simply with butter or Parmesan cheese; serve as a side dish as a collector for the main course's sauces; or use as a base for other recipes.

notes: Water consistency guide: Very soft polenta = 12 cups water; Soft = 10 cups; Medium = 8 cups; Very firm = 6 cups

recipes.title: Basic Fat-Burning Soup
recipes.description: Low-calorie vegetable soup popular in the cabbage soup diet.

instructions.text: Cut vegetables in small pieces and cover with water.
Season with salt and pepper, parsley and, if desired, curry, bouillon or hot sauce.
Boil 10 minutes.
Add onion soup mix; reduce to simmer and continue cooking until vegetables are tender.

notes: Popular 1990s diet soup
Can add other low-calorie vegetables as desired

recipes.title: Polenta Dumplings with Mushrooms and Taleggio
recipes.description: Baked polenta cubes topped with sautéed oyster mushrooms, Taleggio cheese, and browned butter.

ingredients.prep_note: cut into 1-inch cubes (leftover or prepackaged may be used)
brushed and cut into fine strips

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a small, shallow baking dish.
Drop polenta into salted boiling water; cook for 5 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil in an 8-inch skillet over medium heat; fry garlic until golden brown. Discard garlic.
Add mushrooms and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, for 3 minutes. If the mushrooms are dry, add a few tablespoons of water to the skillet.
Add parsley and pepper, cover and reduce heat. Cook for 15 minutes.
Spread mushrooms across the bottom of prepared baking dish. Cover with polenta in an even layer. Top with cheese.
Bake until heated through, about 20 minutes.
Remove from oven and allow to rest 5 minutes.
Melt butter in a small pan. Heat to sizzling, then pour over the polenta and mushrooms.

notes: Taleggio is a semi-soft Italian cheese - can substitute fontina or brie if unavailable

recipes.title: Sauerkraut Surprise Cake
recipes.description: Moist chocolate cake with a secret ingredient - sauerkraut! Topped with sour cream-chocolate frosting.

instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar until light.
Beat in eggs, one at a time, add vanilla.
Sift together flour, baking powder, soda, salt and cocoa powder.
Add dry ingredients to creamed mixture alternately with water, beating after each addition.
Stir in sauerkraut.
Turn into greased and floured 9-by-13-inch pan.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool in pan. Frost when cool.

notes: The sauerkraut adds moisture and texture - no one will guess the secret ingredient!
Includes Sour Cream-Chocolate Frosting recipe

frosting_recipe.title: Sour Cream-Chocolate Frosting
frosting_recipe.instructions: Melt chocolate chips and butter over low heat. Remove from heat; blend in sour cream, vanilla and salt. Gradually add powdered sugar to make spreading consistency, beat well.

recipes.title: Millet Pilaf with Nuts
recipes.description: Aromatic millet pilaf with cinnamon and toasted nuts - serve hot or at room temperature.

instructions.text: Heat butter and olive oil in a heavy saucepan. Add onion; cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until soft and starting to color.
Add cinnamon and millet; cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in water or stock; add salt and white pepper. Bring to a boil, cover and cook over very low heat for about 25 minutes, until the millet is tender and all the liquid has been absorbed.
Uncover and let sit for a few minutes to let the steam escape, then fluff with a fork.
Heat vegetable oil in a small skillet; add nuts. When they start to turn golden, remove pan from heat, lift nuts out with a slotted spoon and drain on absorbent paper.
With a fork, stir half of the nuts through the millet pilaf, then sprinkle the remaining nuts over the top.
Serve hot with a vegetable accompaniment such as beans in tomato sauce. In warm weather, serve the pilaf at room temperature with a salad such as tomato and spring onion.

notes: Vegetable stock is easily obtained by reserving the water used to cook vegetables for your daily meals

recipes.title: Creme de Menthe (Homemade)
recipes.description: Homemade mint liqueur that steeps for 10 days - smooth and refreshing.

instructions.text: Combine vodka, mint essence or extract and mint leaves.
Steep 10 days in a cool, dark place.
Strain through cheesecloth.
Add syrup and glycerine, if used.
Let rest overnight before serving.

notes: Glycerine adds body and smoothness to homemade liqueurs
Add green food coloring if desired

recipes.title: Hoppin' George
recipes.description: A twist on traditional Hoppin' John using pearled barley instead of rice with black-eyed peas.

ingredients.item: bacon bits or chopped cooked bacon

instructions.text: Saute onion and barley in oil until barley is slightly brown, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add black-eyed peas, stock, bacon and salt.
Cover tightly and simmer until tender, about 1 hour.

notes: Traditional Southern New Year's dish variant
Barley adds a chewy, nutty texture different from rice

recipes.title: Alegria (Amaranth Candy)
recipes.description: Traditional Mexican candy made with popped amaranth seeds coated in honey and molasses.

ingredients.item: vegetable oil or nonstick cooking spray
light molasses or dark corn syrup

instructions.text: Pop amaranth by placing in a very hot skillet 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly for about 15 seconds until seeds pop.

recipes.description: Classic Southern pecan pie with Karo syrup.

instructions.text: Mix ingredients in preceding order.
Bake at 400°F for 15 minutes, then at 350°F for 35 to 45 minutes, or until silver knife inserted comes out clean.

recipes.title: Cauliflower Layer Salad
recipes.description: A layered vegetable salad with cauliflower, lettuce, and Parmesan cheese.

instructions.text: In a 9x12 inch dish: Use 1 layer of broken pieces of lettuce, 1 layer of cauliflower pieces, 1 layer of red onion, 1 layer of frozen peas, and 1 layer Parmesan cheese (grated).
Seal top with approximately 2 cups mayonnaise.
Set in refrigerator for overnight.
Toss when ready to serve.

notes: Make ahead - refrigerate overnight

recipes.title: Cherry Cream Cheese Salad
recipes.description: A sweet gelatin salad with pineapple, cherries, and cream cheese.

instructions.text: Heat slowly pineapple, sugar, and gelatin.
Cool completely.
Add cherries, cherry juice, softened cream cheese, and Cool Whip. Nuts are optional.
Let set in refrigerator until firm.

notes: Heat pineapple mixture thoroughly to begin thickening; it will thicken more when cooled

recipes.title: Coleslaw
recipes.description: Classic creamy coleslaw with celery and mustard seed.

instructions.text: Mix spices, sugar, vinegar, and Miracle Whip and let stand in refrigerator a couple of hours before serving.
Then pour over shredded cabbage and carrot.
Can also be used for potato salad - just add eggs, pickles, etc.

notes: Dressing can be used for potato salad too

recipes.title: Cranberry Salad
recipes.description: A festive gelatin salad with cranberry, pineapple, and sour cream.

instructions.text: [INFERRED] Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water.
[INFERRED] Add frozen berries, pineapple, and cranberry sauce.
[INFERRED] Pour half into mold, chill until set.
[INFERRED] Spread sour cream over set layer.
[INFERRED] Top with remaining gelatin mixture and nuts.
[INFERRED] Chill until firm.

notes: Recipe continues on next page - instructions partially inferred

flags.issue: Recipe continues on next page

recipes.title: Spicy Minestrone
recipes.description: Hearty Italian vegetable soup with hamburger, beans, zucchini, and pasta.

ingredients.prep_note: cut in quarters lengthwise, then sliced

instructions.text: Brown hamburger, onion, and garlic in Dutch oven. Drain all but 1 tablespoon fat.
Add potatoes and bell pepper; cook 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes with their liquid, herbs, spices, and pepper flakes, beef stock, salt, and pepper to taste.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes.
Stir in kidney beans with their liquid, zucchini, and pasta. Simmer until pasta is tender, about 20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper if needed. Pass cheese with the soup and let guests help themselves.

recipes.title: Steak Soup
recipes.description: Hearty slow-cooker beef and vegetable soup thickened with a roux.

instructions.text: Cook, covered, on LOW for 8 to 10 hours.
One hour before serving time, turn on HIGH.
Mix together 1/2 cup flour and 1/2 cup oleo, melted, until smooth.
Add to crock pot. Cook until thickened.

notes: Cook in Crock Pot

recipes.title: Broccoli Mushroom Salad
recipes.description: Fresh broccoli and mushroom salad with a tangy homemade dressing.

instructions.text: Wash and slice fresh mushrooms. Break off florets from head of broccoli.
Combine with chopped onions.
[INFERRED] Combine dressing ingredients and toss with vegetables.

notes: Recipe continues on next page - dressing directions partially inferred

flags.issue: Recipe continues on next page

recipes.title: Hot Sausage Soup
recipes.description: Hearty sausage soup with potatoes, corn, beans, and cabbage.

instructions.text: Saute sausage and onions. Add potatoes and enough water to cover.
Cook till tender.
Add corn, beans, juice, and cabbage. Cook till cabbage is done.
More juice can be added if desired.

recipes.title: Jacob's Pottage
recipes.description: Authentic Biblical-style lentil and rice stew - as food Esau bought!

ingredients.item: large dry onions (or leeks with green stalks)

instructions.text: Soak lentils and rice in large soup kettle for several hours. Keep water 1 inch above mixture.
When ready to cook, saute chopped onions in oil.
Add to boiling lentil-rice mixture. Add bouillon.
Cook until rice is soft. Serve thick, hot or cold.
Drop into pita/pocket bread.

notes: Biblical recipe - what Esau traded his birthright for

recipes.title: Potato-Cheese Soup
recipes.description: Creamy pureed potato soup with sharp cheddar cheese.

ingredients.prep_note: peeled and cut into 1/2 inch cubes (2 cups)

instructions.text: In large saucepan, place potatoes, water, carrot, celery, bouillon, and pepper.
Over medium-high heat, bring to a boil; reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Place 1/2 in a blender container or food processor bowl; cover. Blend or process until smooth.
Return to saucepan. Add cheese. Cook and stir over medium heat until cheese melts.
To serve, sprinkle with parsley.

recipes.title: French Onion Soup (Quick)
recipes.description: Quick French onion soup using frozen onions and canned broth.

instructions.text: Empty package of frozen onions into saucepan and heat until they brown lightly. (Do not add butter - as they thaw they brown in their own water.)
Add to onions 1 can bouillon and 1 can consomme. Do not dilute soup.
Heat mixture until blended; remove and let cool. If made ahead of time, refrigerate until ready to serve.
Toast 2 slices of bread and cut into halves.
Pour soup mixture into 4 ovenproof bowls. Add 1/2 slice toast.
Over toast, sprinkle Swiss cheese. Top with American.
Place soup bowls under broiler about 5 minutes, or until brown.
Remove and serve.

recipes.title: French Onion Soup
recipes.description: Classic French onion soup with deeply caramelized onions and Gruyere cheese.

instructions.text: In Dutch oven, heat butter and oil over medium heat. Add onions, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper; stir.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions begin to soften, about 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until onions are caramelized, about 1 hour and 15 minutes.
After 30 minutes, the onions should be light golden brown, 30 to 45 minutes later, onions should be a deep brown.
Stir flour into onions; bring to a bubble. Cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Slowly stir in broth, water, and brandy. Simmer, partially covered, about 15 minutes.
Add salt and pepper if needed. Heat oven to 325°F.
Cut bread into 4 thick slices. Place on baking sheet and bake until dry, about 6 minutes per side.
Pour soup into heatproof bowls. Put a piece of bread on top of each and mount cheese on bread.
Place in broiler until golden brown (2 to 3 minutes).

recipes.title: Hamburger Soup
recipes.description: Easy hamburger and vegetable soup with macaroni.

instructions.text: Brown and drain ground beef.
Add dry ingredients. Stir in water, sauce, celery, and carrots.
Cover and cook on low for 2 hours.
Cook macaroni. Add to soup.
Stir in Parmesan cheese and serve.

recipes.title: Cream of Broccoli Soup
recipes.description: Creamy pureed broccoli and cauliflower soup.

instructions.text: Puree broccoli and cauliflower.
Melt margarine in medium saucepan; saute onions until soft.
Add flour, stirring constantly. Add broth, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Bring to a boil; add pureed vegetables.
Reduce heat and gradually stir in milk.
Heat thoroughly, but do not boil.

recipes.title: Cod Chowder
recipes.description: New England-style fish chowder with cod, bacon, and clam juice.

instructions.text: Rinse fish with cold water; pat dry with paper towels. Cut fish into 1/2 inch cubes; set aside.
In a small skillet, saute bacon until crisp. Remove bacon from skillet; blot with paper towels and crumble; set aside.
Discard all but 2 tablespoons bacon drippings from skillet. Add onion to skillet; saute until tender but not brown. Remove from heat.
In deep saucepan, combine onion and potatoes. Add water, cover, and bring to gentle boil; reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add fish; cover and bring to boil again. Reduce heat and cook for additional 10 minutes, or until fish and potatoes are done.
In small bowl, combine flour and clam juice; stir with fork until smooth.
Add to fish and potato mixture, stirring constantly to blend flour. Stir in evaporated milk, butter, salt, and white pepper.
Continue heating over medium heat until chowder thickens.
Garnish with crumbled bacon before serving.

recipes.title: Cold Strawberry Soup
recipes.description: A sweet, refreshing cold soup perfect for summer - more like a dessert!

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a large bowl, stirring well.
Transfer half to a container of an electric blender and process until almost smooth.
Repeat procedure with remaining mixture. Serve immediately.

notes: May use vanilla ice cream in place of strawberry

recipes.title: Karen's Baked Beans
recipes.description: Hearty baked beans with hamburger, bacon, and three kinds of beans.

instructions.text: Brown hamburger and bacon. Add onion and cook.
Drain. Add all ingredients and bake, uncovered, at 350°F for 40 minutes.

recipes.title: Broccoli Salad
recipes.description: Classic broccoli salad with bacon, raisins, and sweet dressing.

instructions.text: Combine broccoli, bacon, raisins, and red onion.
Combine mayonnaise, sugar, and vinegar to form a sauce and pour over the salad.
Chill overnight.

recipes.title: Broccoli Casserole
recipes.description: Cheesy broccoli and rice casserole with mushrooms.

instructions.text: Cook rice to make 1 cup. Cook broccoli and drain.
In large skillet, put oleo. Saute the onion, but not brown.
Put in the Cheddar cheese soup, the mushrooms, and juice.
Blend in rice and broccoli.
Pour mixture in buttered baking dish. Sprinkle top with crumbled onion rings.
Bake at 325°F for 35 minutes or until bubbly.

recipes.title: Marinated Broccoli
recipes.description: Fresh vegetable salad marinated in a tangy herb dressing.

instructions.text: Mix together vinegar, dill weed, salt, sugar, oil, marjoram, garlic, Accent, and pepper and refrigerate.
Combine broccoli, cauliflower, tomatoes, and mushrooms.
Pour dressing over vegetables and marinate.

recipes.title: French Salad Dressing
recipes.description: Homemade French dressing - makes 1 cup.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients and chill. Makes 1 cup of dressing.
