recipes.title: Almost-Famous Broccoli-Cheddar Soup
recipes.source_note: Food Network Magazine - Panera Bread copycat

ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
grated sharp white and yellow cheddar cheese, plus more for garnish

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until tender, about 5 minutes. Whisk in the flour and cook until golden, 3 to 4 minutes, then gradually whisk in the half-and-half until smooth. Add the chicken broth, bay leaves and nutmeg, then season with salt and pepper and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook, uncovered, until thickened, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare the bread bowls: Using a sharp knife, cut a circle into the top of each loaf, leaving a 1-inch border all around. Remove the bread top, then hollow out the middle with a fork or your fingers, leaving a thick bread shell.

Add the broccoli and carrot to the broth mixture and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Discard the bay leaves. Puree the soup in batches in a blender until smooth; you'll still have flecks of carrot and broccoli. Return to the pot. (Or puree the soup in the pot with an immersion blender.)
Add the cheese to the soup and whisk over medium heat until melted. Add up to 3/4 cup water if the soup is too thick. Ladle into the bread bowls and garnish with cheese.

notes: Panera Bread sells over 50 million cups of this soup annually.
Or puree the soup in the pot with an immersion blender.
Add up to 3/4 cup water if the soup is too thick.

recipes.title: Aaron McCargo Jr.'s Steak Fajita Chili

ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
red or green bell pepper, chopped

instructions.text: Heat 1/4 cup canola oil in a large soup pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season the short ribs with salt and pepper and sear until golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer the meat to another large pot (set the first pot aside) and add the broth. Cover and cook until tender, about 1 hour 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 cup oil in the reserved pot over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper, and cumin, chili powder, oregano, flour. Cook, stirring, until the flour is lightly browned and set aside until the meat is done. Add the warm broth and whisk until smooth; cover the broth and set aside.

Transfer the short ribs to a cutting board; cover the broth and set aside. Let the meat cool slightly, then cut into chunks. Place the pot with the vegetables over medium-high heat. Slowly add the warm broth and whisk until smooth. Stir in the chopped short ribs and the beans, bring to a simmer and cook until thickened, about 15 minutes. Ladle into bowls and garnish with guacamole, sour cream, cheese and fried tortilla strips, for a little extra crunch.

notes: Aaron's secret weapon: Short ribs for extra richness.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with guacamole, sour cream, cheese and fried tortilla strips for a little extra crunch.

recipes.title: Tortilla Soup
recipes.source_note: Food Network Magazine - Taco Bell copycat

ingredients.item: diced tomatoes, with dried oregano and salt

instructions.text: Sauté the diced onion, minced jalapeño and garlic cloves in canola oil in a large pot. Add the ground cumin.
Add the low-sodium chicken broth and two 15-ounce cans no-salt canned vegetables.
Stir in lime juice. Meanwhile, toast the tortilla in a 350°F oven until crisp.
Ladle into bowls, garnish with sour cream and some chopped cilantro on top. Crumble the toasted tortilla on top.

recipes.title: Hawaiian Fish Lettuce Wraps
recipes.source_note: Food Network Magazine - BK Big Fish Sandwich copycat

instructions.text: Mix the toppings from a Burger King BK Big Fish Sandwich with 1 packet tartar sauce, 2 tablespoons plain nonfat yogurt and 1 1/2 teaspoons Asian chili sauce.

Sauté 4 slices Canadian bacon in a skillet coated with cooking spray until browned on both sides, then thinly slice. Cut the fish fillet into strips. Divide the fish among 8 Bibb lettuce leaves; top with the corn, coleslaw, bacon and the sauce.
Press sesame seeds onto the cut sides of the bun and sprinkle with salt; cut into strips and toast in a 350°F oven until crisp. Serve with the lettuce wraps.

notes: Using lettuce instead of bread cuts calories significantly.
You can do this for any sandwich to keep calories down.

recipes.title: Asian Chicken Salad

ingredients.item: KFC Breast (with corn, coleslaw and a biscuit)

instructions.text: Discard the chicken skin and shred the meat from a KFC Breast.
Whisk 1 tablespoon each rice vinegar, low-sodium soy sauce, brown sugar, 1 teaspoon grated ginger, 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes and 1 tablespoon sesame oil.
Toss the chicken with the salad. Cut the biscuit into cubes and toss with the salad; pepper to taste. Toast in a 350°F oven until crunchy, then sprinkle over the salad.

notes: The makeover cuts the fat by 80 percent while keeping the Colonel's secret herbs and spices.

recipes.title: Sloppy Joes
recipes.source_note: Food Network Magazine - McDonald's Big Mac healthy makeover by Ellie Krieger
recipes.description: A healthier take on the Big Mac, turning it into sloppy joes with beans and veggies for added lean protein.

instructions.text: Finely chop the filling of a McDonald's Big Mac, including the burger and toppings; reserve the outer buns and discard the center bun. Dice 1/2 onion.

Sauté 1 celery stalk (1/4 cup minced), 1/2 jalapeño and 2 minced garlic cloves in a skillet with 1 tablespoon olive oil until soft, 5 minutes. Add the chopped Big Mac filling, 3/4 cup no-salt red beans, tomato sauce, 2 teaspoons tomato paste, 2 packets ketchup and 1/2 packet hot mustard sauce and simmer 3 minutes.
Spoon onto 4 hamburger buns using the reserved bun and 3 more.

notes: Per serving: Calories 310; Fat 13g (Saturated 3g); Cholesterol 20mg; Sodium 520mg; Carbohydrate 37g; Fiber 5g; Protein 12g
Fat per serving drops from 29 grams to just 13
The beans add lean protein.
Fat per serving drops from 29 grams to just 13.
Spread among four plates to control portions.

recipes.title: Daisy Potato Skins

instructions.text: Lightly grease outside of potatoes. Cut a small slit in top and bake at 425°F for 45 minutes. Cut potatoes in half lengthwise and scoop out cooked potato, leaving a very thin layer of potato interior. (Save cooked potato for mashed potatoes or hash browns.) Brush outside and inside of skins with melted butter. Sprinkle inside with steak seasoning and Parmesan cheese melted. Place on bubbly greased baking sheet. Bake 8 minutes or until crisp and bubbly.

Let stand until cool enough to handle, and scoop out cooked potato, leaving a thin layer. Brush outside and inside of skins with butter. Bake 3 minutes or until cheese is melted. Top each with a dollop of sour cream and sprinkle with chives.

notes: Save cooked potato for mashed potatoes or hash browns.
Brush inside and outside of skins with steak seasoning and Parmesan.

recipes.title: Warm and Creamy Bacon Dip

instructions.text: Bring cream cheese to room temperature. Preheat oven to 400°F. In a bowl, combine all ingredients. Place in 1-quart baking dish. Cover.
Heat 25-30 minutes or until hot. Serve with sliced French bread, crackers and/or chips. Makes 3 cups.

notes: Serving option: Dip may also be placed in hollowed round sourdough loaf, wrapped in foil and heated in 400°F oven for 30 minutes.
Dip may also be placed in hollowed round sourdough loaf, wrapped in foil and heated in 400°F oven for 30 minutes.
Serve with sliced French bread, crackers and/or chips.

recipes.title: Sour Cream Chocolate Cake

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F. In a large mixer bowl, beat vegetable oil, egg, and vanilla for 1 minute at medium speed; add sugars and beat 1 minute; add melted chocolate and beat 1 minute.

In a small bowl, combine flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt, then add to chocolate mixture alternately with water, beating well after each addition. Add sour cream and mix well. Pour into two greased and floured 8-inch round pans and bake 30-35 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes, then remove from pans to cool completely before frosting.

notes: Find the chocolate frosting recipe at daisybrand.com

recipes.title: French Onion Burgers

ingredients.item: Pepperidge Farm Classic Sandwich Buns with Sesame Seeds, split

instructions.text: Shape beef into 4 (1/2-inch thick) burgers.
Heat skillet over medium-high heat. Add burgers and cook until well browned on both sides. Remove burgers from skillet. Pour off fat.

Stir soup in skillet and heat to a boil. Return burgers to skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 5 min. or until desired doneness. Top burgers with cheese and cook until cheese is melted. Serve burgers on buns with soup mixture for dipping.

notes: Top burgers with cheese and cook until cheese is melted.
Serve burgers on buns with soup mixture for dipping.

recipes.title: Very Strawberry Shortcake

ingredients.item: fat free frozen whipped topping, thawed

instructions.text: Shortcake Directions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Stir together biscuit mix and 1/3 cup SPLENDA Granulated Sweetener in a large bowl.
Stir together yogurt and vanilla; add to dry ingredients, stirring just until moistened.

Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface, and knead 3 or 4 times. Pat dough to a 1/2-inch thickness. Cut with a 2 1/4-inch round biscuit cutter, reusing dough scraps if necessary. Place shortcakes on an ungreased baking sheet. Bake 12 to 15 minutes.
Strawberry Filling Directions: Stir together strawberries, 2 tablespoons SPLENDA Granulated Sweetener and balsamic vinegar; let stand 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Serve warm shortcakes with strawberries. Garnish with whipped topping and mint sprigs if desired.

notes: Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead 3 or 4 times. Pat dough to 1/2-inch thickness.
Serve warm with sliced strawberries.

recipes.title: Fresh Whole-Wheat Pitas
recipes.description: These are sublime straight out of the oven and still delicious at room temperature. Arthur Flour makes a white whole wheat flour is available through King Arthur.

instructions.text: Combine flour, Add bread flour, 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons warm water, yeast, sugar, salt, fat free yogurt, oil, and whole wheat flour in a stand mixer. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough on a lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes. Cover with cooking spray.
Place dough in a large bowl, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°F).
Divide dough into 10 portions. Working with one portion at a time, gently roll each into a 6-inch circle. Place 4 at a time heavily coated baking sheet on the lowest oven rack at 500°F.
Bake for 8 minutes or until puffed and browned. Cool on a wire rack. Yield: 8 servings (serving size: 1 pita).

flags: image rotated, some text difficult to read

recipes.title: Southwest Corn Bread
recipes.description: Part of a chili night menu that serves 8.

instructions.text: Combine 1 (8 1/2-ounce package) corn muffin mix (such as Jiffy) and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin in a medium bowl. Combine 1/3 cup 2% reduced-fat milk, 2 tablespoons finely chopped seeded jalapeño pepper, and 1 large egg, stirring with a whisk. Add milk mixture to muffin mix mixture; stir in 1/2 cup reduced-fat shredded Mexican-blend cheese.
Spoon into an 8-inch square baking pan. Bake at 400°F for 25 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.

recipes.title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light - Hearty Weeknight Supper Menu
recipes.description: Roasted Brussels sprouts retain a crisp-tender texture and gain caramelized flavor from browned edges. Choose boil-in-bag brown rice if you're in a hurry; it cooks in about 10 minutes. Menu serves 4.

instructions.text: Cut 1 pound trimmed Brussels sprouts in half lengthwise. Combine Brussels sprouts, 2 tablespoons melted butter, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper on a jelly-roll pan.
Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes or until browned and tender. Remove from oven.
Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon grated lemon rind; toss to combine.

recipes.title: Garlicky Broccoli Rabe
recipes.description: Broccoli rabe's bitterness is a pleasant foil to the sweet spices in the lamb dish. Pour the same wine you used for the lamb. You can make the cookies a couple of days in advance. Menu serves 6.

instructions.text: Cook 8 cups (2-inch) cut broccoli rabe in boiling water 2 minutes or until crisp-tender. Drain and plunge into ice water; drain.

Heat 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper and 4 minced garlic cloves; cook 1 minute, stirring frequently.
Add broccoli rabe and 1/2 teaspoon salt; cook 3 minutes or until heated, stirring occasionally. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Anasazi and Black Bean Chili
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light - Food Trends by Michael Ruhlman
recipes.description: Slightly sweet red-and-white Anasazi beans contrast with robust black beans in flavor and color. You can substitute pinto beans for the Anasazi beans if you prefer.

instructions.text: Sort and wash Anasazi beans; place in a large bowl. Cover with water to 2 inches above beans. Cover and let stand 8 hours. Drain and set aside.
Place Anasazi beans in a large saucepan; cover with water to 2 inches above. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 50 minutes or until tender. Drain.
Repeat procedure with black beans.
Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray. Add onion and next 5 ingredients (through garlic); sauté 5 minutes.

Add ingredients: Add beans, broth, and next 5 ingredients (through tomatoes); bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 35 minutes. Stir in chorizo; simmer 5 minutes. Serve with sour cream and chopped onion, if desired. Yield: 8 servings.

recipes.title: Herbed Heritage Pork Loin with White Wine Reduction
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light - Food Trends (Meat with Approval)
recipes.description: We find Berkshire pork tender and juicy yet milder than the more robust Duroc. Both varieties are forgiving—partly because of their even marbling, the meat remains succulent even if slightly overcooked.

ingredients.item: boneless heritage pork loin, trimmed (such as Berkshire or Duroc)

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Sprinkle first 3 ingredients over pork; rub over pork.

Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet. Add pork to pan, cook 7 minutes, browning on all sides. Place pork in a broiler pan coated with cooking spray. Bake at 425°F for 35 minutes or until thermometer registers 155°F (slightly pink). Remove pork to a cutting board. Cover loosely with foil; let stand 10 minutes.

Place roasting pan over medium heat. Add shallots to pan; cook 2 minutes. Add wine, scraping pan to loosen browned bits; bring to a boil. Cook until mixture is reduced to 1/2 cup (about 3 minutes). Add chicken broth and orange juice; cook until mixture is reduced to 3/4 cup (about 3 minutes).
Slice pork. Serve with sauce.

recipes.title: Lemon-Salmon Salad Sandwiches
recipes.description: Look for salmon in pouches in the canned fish section of the supermarket. A hearty white bread has sufficient heft to stand up to the sandwich filling. Slices from a bakery artisan loaf would dress up the sandwich even more.

instructions.text: Finely grate 1 teaspoon lemon rind; squeeze 3 tablespoons juice from lemon over a medium bowl. Add rind, mayonnaise, and pepper to bowl; stir well. Let stand 5 minutes. Add salmon to bowl; stir until well blended.
Layer cucumber evenly over 4 bread slices; top each with about 1/4 cup salmon mixture. Top with remaining 4 bread slices. Yield: 4 servings (serving size: 1 sandwich).

recipes.title: Balsamic Pork with Shallots
recipes.description: This dish is reminiscent of bistro-style steak with shallot sauce. Serve with rice, egg noodles, or roasted potatoes.
recipes.servings_yield: 4 servings (serving size: 3 ounces pork and 1/4 cup shallot mixture)

ingredients.item: pork tenderloin, trimmed and cut crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick slices

instructions.text: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Sprinkle pork with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add pork to pan; cook 3 minutes on each side or until done. Remove from pan, and keep warm.

Add remaining 4 teaspoons oil to pan; reduce heat to medium. Add shallots to pan; cook 10 minutes or until tender, stirring occasionally. Add garlic; cook 2 minutes. Stir in 1/2 cup water and vinegar; simmer 6 minutes. Stir in remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and remaining 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Spoon shallot mixture over pork. Serve immediately. Yield: 4 servings.

recipes.title: Paprika Pork
recipes.description: Assorted colors of fresh peppers and paprika turn bottled marinara into a rich Hungarian goulash-style sauce for a quick, hearty weeknight supper.
recipes.servings_yield: 4 servings (serving size: 3/4 cup pork mixture and 3/4 cup noodles)

ingredients.item: pork tenderloin, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
cups red wine pasta sauce (such as Cabernet)
cups hot cooked egg noodles (about 2 cups uncooked)

instructions.text: Heat a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray.
Add bell peppers to pan; sauté 5 minutes or until tender. Remove from pan.

Coat pan with cooking spray. Sprinkle pork with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper; add pork to pan; cook 4 minutes, browning on all sides. Add paprika; cook 1 minute. Add pasta sauce, 1/4 teaspoon salt, remaining black pepper, and 3 tablespoons water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 25 minutes or until meat is tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Serve over egg noodles. Yield: 4 servings.

recipes.title: Sausage and Roasted Pepper Pasta
recipes.description: Four assertive ingredients tossed with mild pasta make for a simple, satisfying supper. Fry in this recipe Bell peppers in a thin red-and-green sauce.

instructions.text: Preheat broiler.

Cut bell peppers in half lengthwise; discard seeds and membranes. Place pepper halves, skin sides up, on a foil-lined baking sheet; flatten with hand. Broil 10 minutes or until blackened. Place in a plastic bag. Let stand 15 minutes. Peel and cut into strips.
Cook pasta according to package directions, omitting salt and fat. Drain.

Remove casings from sausage. Cook sausage in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until browned, stirring to crumble. Add pepper strips, tomato paste, salt, and black pepper; cook 1 minute. Serve over pasta; sprinkle with cheese.

recipes.title: Albuquerque Turkey
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light - Reader Recipe by Lauri Short

ingredients.item: frozen pepper stir-fry (such as Bird's Eye)
sodium-free chicken fat-free, less-sodium chicken broth
boneless, skinless chicken breast, trimmed and cut into 3/4-inch pieces

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add pepper stir-fry to pan; sauté, stirring occasionally.
Add carrots; sauté 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add chiles and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 15 minutes or until rice is tender, and broth is absorbed.
Place one-third of broth mixture in blender lid (to allow steam to escape); puree until smooth. Pour into a large bowl. Repeat procedure with remaining broth mixture. Return to pan.

Add remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper; stir in remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper to pan; reduce heat, and simmer 5 minutes or until thickened, stirring occasionally. Stir in tablespoons (about 4 meatballs) into broth mixture. Add remaining broth to a boil. Drop meat mixture by rounded tablespoons into broth mixture. Cook 3 minutes or until meatballs are done. Combine chicken, pork, 1/4 teaspoon salt, remaining broth mixture, cilantro, 1/4 cup rice, 1/4 teaspoon salt.

recipes.title: Monday Morning Potato Rolls and Bread
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Reader Recipe by Catherine McMichael, Saginaw, Mich.
recipes.description: I make a fairly traditional Sunday meal of chicken and potatoes for my family. I hated to see the leftovers go to waste, so I used the mashed potatoes to create these delicious rolls. I experimented with 10 variations before settling on this version. My kids and husband love the rolls so much that they never last until Tuesday!
recipes.servings_yield: 18 servings (serving size: 1 roll or one-ninth of loaf)

ingredients.item: mashed cooked peeled baking potatoes (about 8 ounces)

instructions.text: Combine first 4 ingredients in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave at HIGH for 2 minutes or until mixture is 110°F. Stir with a whisk until smooth.

Weigh or lightly spoon flour into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Combine 6.75 ounces (about 1 1/2 cups) flour, yeast, and salt in a large mixing bowl. Add potato mixture to flour mixture, stirring with a fork until combined. Add eggs; stir until combined.

Add 9 ounces (about 2 cups) flour to potato mixture; stir until a soft dough forms. Turn dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 10 minutes); add enough of remaining 1/2 cup flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, to prevent dough from sticking to hands (dough will feel sticky).

Place dough in a large bowl coated with olive oil, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°F), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If indentation remains, dough has risen enough.) Punch dough down; cover and let rest 5 minutes.

Divide dough in half. Working with one portion at a time (cover remaining dough to prevent drying), roll one portion into a 14 x 7-inch rectangle on a floured surface. Roll up rectangle tightly, starting with a short edge, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets; pinch seam and ends to seal. Place loaf, seam side down, in an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray.

Shape remaining portion into 9 portions, and shape each into a ball. Place balls in an 8-inch square baking dish coated with cooking spray. Coat top of loaf and rolls with cooking spray. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°F), free from drafts, 30 minutes or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If the indentation remains, dough has risen enough.)
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes or until tops of rolls are browned and loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. Remove from pans; cool on wire racks. Yield: 18 servings.

recipes.title: Creamy Carrot Soup
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Reader Recipe by Lisa Richardson, Glendale, Calif.
recipes.description: I prepared this soup for my parents, who watch my daughter one afternoon a week. They absolutely loved its velvety sweetness. Garnish with shredded carrot and fresh mint.

ingredients.item: chopped Vidalia or other sweet onion

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and carrots to pan; cook 10 minutes, stirring frequently. Stir in salt, pepper, and ginger.
Add 2 cups water and broth to pan; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 25 minutes or until carrots are tender. Remove from heat; cool.

Place half of carrot mixture and 1 tablespoon cream in a food processor or blender; process 20 seconds or until smooth. Pour pureed mixture into a large bowl. Repeat procedure with remaining carrot mixture and 1 tablespoon cream. Return mixture to pan; cook over medium heat until thoroughly heated. Yield: 4 servings.

notes: CALORIES 180; FAT 6.9g (sat 2.3g, mono 3.3g, poly 0.9g); PROTEIN 3.5g; CARB 28.7g; FIBER 7.6g; CHOL 10mg; IRON 0.9mg; SODIUM 963mg; CALC 97mg

recipes.title: Swanson Pan Sautéed Chicken with Vegetables and Herbs

ingredients.item: large red onions, cut into quarters
fresh whole baby carrots (about 16), green tops trimmed to 1 inch

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Combine black pepper, paprika and flour. Coat the chicken with flour mixture.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until it's well browned on all sides. Remove the chicken from the skillet.
Add the onions and potatoes to the skillet and cook for 5 minutes. Add the carrots, stock, lemon juice and oregano and heat to a boil. Return the chicken to the skillet. Cover the skillet.
Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes. Uncover the skillet and bake for 15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender. Sprinkle with the thyme.

recipes.title: Deep Dark Chocolate Biscotti
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Reader Recipe by Linda Rogers, Manistee, Mich.
recipes.description: Whole-wheat flour, flaxseed, and almonds add fiber and antioxidants.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Weigh or lightly spoon flour into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Combine flour, flaxseed, soda, and salt in a bowl, stirring with a whisk. Combine sugars, egg whites, and egg in a bowl; beat with a mixer at high speed for 2 minutes. Add vanilla; mix well. Add flour mixture to egg mixture; stir until combined. Fold in chocolate and almonds. Divide dough into 3 equal portions. Roll each portion into a 6-inch-long roll. Arrange rolls 3 inches apart on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Pat to a 1-inch thickness. Bake at 350°F for 28 minutes or until firm.

Remove rolls from baking sheet; cool 10 minutes on a wire rack. Cut rolls diagonally into 30 (1/2-inch) slices. Place, cut sides down, on baking sheet. Reduce oven temperature to 325°F; bake 7 minutes. Turn cookies over; bake 7 minutes (cookies will be slightly soft in center but will harden as they cool). Remove from baking sheet; cool on wire rack. Yield: 2 1/2 dozen.

notes: CALORIES 94; FAT 2.3g (sat 0.8g, mono 1.1g, poly 0.3g); PROTEIN 2.1g; CARB 14.4g; FIBER 1.1g; CHOL 7mg; IRON 0.9mg; SODIUM 49mg; CALC 18mg

recipes.title: Broccoli and Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light - Lighten Up by Kathy Kitchens Downie, RD
recipes.description: If the broccoli florets are large, break into smaller pieces at the stalk instead of chopping them; they'll cook more quickly. Count on having dinner on the table in about 40 minutes, and serve this soup the moment it's done for the best results. In fact, if you wait, you'll find it gets thicker with time. If you have leftovers, you will want to thin the soup with a little chicken broth or milk to the desired consistency.

ingredients.item: shredded light processed cheese (such as Velveeta Light)

instructions.text: Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray. Add onion, mushrooms, and garlic to pan; sauté 5 minutes or until liquid evaporates, stirring occasionally. Reduce heat to medium; add butter to mushroom mixture, stirring until butter melts. Sprinkle mushroom mixture with flour; cook 2 minutes, stirring occasionally. Gradually add milk and broth, stirring constantly with a whisk; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low; cook 10 minutes or until slightly thick, stirring constantly.

Add pasta to pan; cook 10 minutes. Add cheese to pan, and stir until cheese melts. Add chicken and remaining ingredients to pan; cook 5 minutes or until broccoli is tender and soup is thoroughly heated. Yield: 10 servings.

notes: Before: CALORIES 534, TOTAL FAT 33g, SATURATED FAT 18.6g, SODIUM 1,289mg
After: CALORIES 317, TOTAL FAT 12.3g, SATURATED FAT 6.8g, SODIUM 723mg
If the broccoli florets are large, break into smaller pieces at the stalk instead of chopping them; they'll cook more quickly.
Count on having dinner on the table in about 40 minutes.
Serve this soup the moment it's done for the best results. In fact, if you wait, you'll find it gets thicker with time.
If you have leftovers, you will want to thin the soup with a little chicken broth or milk to the desired consistency.

recipes.title: Bucatini alla Carbonara
recipes.description: Ragù alla Bolognese sauces are popular throughout Italy. The most prominent, even among residents of the city from which it hails, is cured pork. Bucatini is hollow spaghetti; guanciale (gwahn-CHAY-lay) is cured pork.

ingredients.item: guanciale; cook until crisp, stirring frequently. Remove pan from heat. Add guanciale; cook until crisp from heat

instructions.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add guanciale; cook until crisp, stirring frequently. Remove from heat.
Bring 6 quarts water and salt to a boil in an 8-quart pot. Add pasta; cook until al dente. Remove from heat. Drain pasta over a bowl, reserving 3/4 cup pasta water. Return pasta to pot.

Combine cheese and next 3 ingredients (through eggs) in a bowl, stirring well. Add cheese mixture to pasta; toss to combine. Place pasta mixture over low heat. Cook 5 minutes or until thick, stirring constantly. (Do not overheat; sauce will curdle.) Add reserved pasta water, 1/4 cup at a time, tossing to combine. Place remaining cheese on each of 6 plates; top each serving with 1/4 cup reserved pasta. Sprinkle with pepper.

recipes.title: Fettuccine with Olive Oil, Garlic, and Red Pepper

instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic; cook 2 minutes. Stir in red pepper.

Cook pasta according to package directions; drain, reserving 1/2 cup pasta water. Add pasta to pan; toss to combine. Place pasta on each of 6 plates; drizzle each serving with 1 teaspoon remaining oil. Yield: 6 servings.

recipes.title: Tagliatelle alla Bolognese
recipes.description: Meat-based pasta sauces are popular throughout Italy. The most prominent, ragù alla Bolognese, originated in the northern city of Bologna. Even among residents of the city from which it hails, different variations abound.

instructions.text: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-heat. Add pancetta to pan, and cook 2 minutes. Add chopped onion, chopped carrot and celery. Add veal, ground pork, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and pepper; cook 5 minutes or until browned, stirring occasionally. Add wine. Cook 3 minutes or until liquid almost evaporates, stirring to crumble. Reduce heat to medium-low.

Stir in tomato paste, stirring occasionally until ground veal, ground pork, 1 teaspoon salt, and pepper; cook 5 minutes or until browned. Add wine. Cook 3 minutes or until liquid almost evaporates. Reduce heat to medium-low.

Place parsley sprigs and next 3 ingredients (through cloves) on a double layer of cheesecloth. Gather edges of cheesecloth together; tie securely. Add cheesecloth bag and milk to pan; bring to a simmer. Simmer on low heat 1 hour or until thick, stirring occasionally. Discard cheesecloth bag.

Bring 6 quarts water to a boil in an 8-quart pot. Add pasta; salt to pot. Stir. Cover; return water to a boil. Uncover and cook 8 minutes or until al dente. Drain. Place 1 cup pasta in each of 6 shallow bowls; spoon about 1/4 cup sauce over each serving. Sprinkle each with 1 tablespoon chopped parsley. Yield: 6 servings.

notes: WINE NOTE: A pasta with Bolognese sauce needs a wine that will balance the richness of the pork, veal, and pancetta, plus mirror the acidity of the tomato paste. A wine made from sangiovese grapes—such as Chianti—is ideally balanced. Opt specifically for a Chianti Classico, which is richer and earthier than basic Chianti. A great wine for the price is Chianti Classico 2005 ($14). —Karen MacNeil

recipes.title: Fresh Tomato Sauce
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light - Cooking Class (How to make fresh tomato sauce)
recipes.description: Fresh tomato sauce is a staple in Italy, where it's usually served with spaghetti. Although the sauce tastes rich and delicious, it only takes about 30 minutes to prepare.

instructions.text: To peel tomatoes, core and cut a small X through the skin on the bottom of tomatoes with a sharp knife. Place them in boiling water for about 30 seconds or just until skins begin to peel back. Quickly remove tomatoes from pan, and plunge them into ice water. Drain and remove skins. Cut each tomato in half lengthwise, and squeeze the juices and seeds into a colander over a bowl. Reserve tomato juices, and discard seeds. Finely chop tomatoes.
Heat extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic, and cook just until it begins to brown lightly, taking care not to burn it.
Add tomatoes and reserved juices, and cook until almost all of the liquid evaporates.

Finish cooking the pasta with the sauce, which should be in a skillet large enough to combine the two and allow for tossing. Add enough of the pasta cooking water to the sauce to give the dish a creamy texture and marry the sauce to the pasta.

notes: See full recipe on page 138 of Cooking Light March 2009

recipes.title: Sloppy Joes (Big Mac Makeover)
recipes.source_note: Food Network Magazine - Ellie Krieger, McDonald's Big Mac makeover

instructions.text: Finely chop the filling of a McDonald's Big Mac, including the burger patties and toppings; reserve the outer buns and discard the center bun. Dice the onion.
Sauté in a skillet with 1 tablespoon olive oil until soft, 5 minutes. Add the chopped Big Mac filling, red beans, tomato sauce, tomato paste, ketchup and hot mustard sauce and simmer 3 minutes.
Spoon onto 4 hamburger buns using the reserved bun and 3 more.

notes: Per serving: Calories 310; Fat 13g; Saturated 3g; Cholesterol 20mg; Sodium 520mg; Carbohydrate 37g; Fiber 5g; Protein 12g

instructions.text: Lightly grease outside of potatoes. Cut a small slit in top and bake at 425°F for 45 minutes or until soft. Let stand until cool enough to handle. Cut potatoes in half lengthwise and scoop out cooked potato, leaving a very thin layer of potato interior. (Save cooked potato for mashed potatoes or hash browns.) Brush outside and inside of skins with melted butter. Sprinkle inside with steak seasoning and Parmesan cheese.

Place on lightly greased baking sheet. Bake 8 minutes or until crisp and bubbly. Place Cheddar cheese and bacon. Bake 3 minutes or until cheese is melted. Top each with a dollop of sour cream and sprinkle with chives.
Bring cream cheese to room temperature. Preheat oven to 400°F. In a bowl, combine all ingredients. Place in 1-quart baking dish. Cover.
Heat 25-30 minutes or until hot. Serve with sliced French bread, crackers and/or chips. Makes 3 cups.
Serving option: Dip may also be placed in hollowed round sourdough loaf, wrapped in foil and heated in 400°F oven for 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°F. In a large mixer bowl, beat vegetable oil, egg and vanilla for 1 minute at medium speed; add sugars and beat 1 minute; add melted chocolate and beat 1 minute.

In a small bowl, combine flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt, then add to chocolate mixture alternately with water, beating well after each addition. Add sour cream and mix well. Pour into two greased and floured 8-inch round pans and bake 30-35 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes, then remove from pans to cool completely before frosting.

ingredients.item: Pepperidge Farm Classic Sandwich Buns with Sesame Seeds, split

instructions.text: Shape beef into 4 (1/2-inch thick) burgers.
Heat skillet over medium-high heat. Add burgers and cook until well browned on both sides. Remove burgers from skillet. Pour off fat.

Stir soup in skillet and heat to a boil. Return burgers to skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 5 min. or until desired doneness. Top burgers with cheese and cook until cheese is melted. Serve burgers on buns with soup mixture for dipping.

ingredients.item: fat free frozen whipped topping, thawed

instructions.text: Combine biscuit mix and 1/3 cup SPLENDA Granulated Sweetener in a large bowl.
Stir together yogurt and vanilla; add to dry ingredients, stirring just until moistened.

Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead 3 or 4 times. Pat dough to a 1/2-inch thickness. Cut with a 2 1/4-inch round biscuit cutter, re-using dough scraps if necessary. Place shortcakes on an ungreased baking sheet. Bake 12 to 15 minutes.
Strawberry Filling Directions: Stir together strawberries, 2 tablespoons SPLENDA Granulated Sweetener and balsamic vinegar; let stand 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Shortcake Directions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Serve warm shortcakes with Strawberry Filling. Garnish: 1/4 cups strawberries, 14 cups shredded coconut frozen.
Knife: Add bread flour, 3 ounces about 3/4 cup, whole wheat flour, yogurt, oil, and salt to the yeast mixture; stir with a whisk.

Divide dough into 8 portions. Working with one portion at a time, gently roll each portion into a 6 inch circle. Place 4 dough circles on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray. Bake at 500° for 8 minutes or until golden and puffed. Repeat with remaining dough.
Preheat the oven to 500°.
Use of unbleached flour is available through King Arthur Flour (www.bakerscatalogue.com).

recipes.title: Southwest Corn Bread
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Chili Night menu

instructions.text: Combine 1 (8 1/2-ounce package) corn muffin mix (such as Jiffy) and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin in a medium bowl. Combine 1/3 cup 2% reduced-fat milk, 2 tablespoons finely chopped seeded jalapeño pepper, and 1 large egg, stirring with a whisk. Add milk mixture to muffin mix mixture; stir in 1/2 cup reduced-fat shredded Mexican-blend cheese.
Spoon into an 8-inch square baking pan. Bake at 400° for 25 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.

recipes.title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Hearty Weeknight Supper menu

instructions.text: Cut 1 pound trimmed Brussels sprouts in half lengthwise. Combine Brussels sprouts, 2 tablespoons melted butter, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper on a jelly-roll pan.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes or until browned and tender. Remove from oven. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon grated lemon rind; toss to combine.

recipes.title: Garlicky Broccoli Rabe
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Dinner Party menu

instructions.text: Cook 8 cups (2-inch) cut broccoli rabe in boiling water 2 minutes or until crisp-tender. Drain and plunge into ice water; drain.

Heat 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper and 4 minced garlic cloves; cook 1 minute, stirring frequently.
Add broccoli rabe and 1/2 teaspoon salt; cook 3 minutes or until heated, stirring occasionally. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Anasazi and Black Bean Chili
recipes.servings_yield: 12 servings (serving size: 3 ounces pork and 1 tablespoon sauce)

instructions.text: Sort and wash Anasazi beans; place in a large bowl. Cover with water to 2 inches above beans. Cover and let stand 8 hours. Drain beans; place in a large saucepan. Cover with water to 2 inches above beans. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 50 minutes or until tender. Drain.
Repeat procedure with black beans.
Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray. Add onion and next 5 ingredients (through garlic); sauté 5 minutes.

Add ingredients: Add beans, broth, and next 5 ingredients; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 35 minutes. Stir in chorizo; simmer 5 minutes. Serve with sour cream and chopped onion. Serve immediately. Yield: 8 servings (serving size: 1 1/3 cups chili).

recipes.title: Herbed Heritage Pork Loin with White Wine Reduction
recipes.description: We find Berkshire pork tender and juicy yet milder than the more robust Duroc. Both varieties are forgiving—partly because of their even marbling, the meat remains succulent even if slightly overcooked.

ingredients.item: trimmed boneless heritage pork loin (such as Berkshire pork or Duroc)

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 425°.
Sprinkle first 3 ingredients over pork; rub coriander mixture evenly over pork. Combine parsley and next 4 ingredients (through thyme); rub herb mixture over pork.

Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork to pan; cook 7 minutes, browning on all sides. Place pork in a broiler pan coated with cooking spray. Bake at 425° for 35 minutes or until thermometer registers 155° (slightly pink). Remove pork to a cutting board. Cover loosely with foil; let stand 10 minutes.

Place roasting pan over medium heat. Add shallots to pan; cook 2 minutes, scraping pan to loosen browned bits; bring to a boil. Cook until mixture is reduced to 3/4 cup (about 3 minutes). Add chicken broth and orange juice; cook until mixture is reduced to 3/4 cup.

recipes.title: Lemon-Salmon Salad Sandwiches
recipes.description: Look for salmon in pouches in the canned fish section of the supermarket. A hearty white bread has sufficient heft to stand up to the sandwich filling. Slices from a bakery artisan loaf would dress up the sandwich even more.

instructions.text: Finely grate 1 teaspoon lemon rind; squeeze 3 tablespoons juice from lemon over a medium bowl. Add rind, mayonnaise, and pepper to bowl; stir well. Let stand 5 minutes. Add salmon to bowl; stir until well blended.
Layer cucumber evenly over 4 bread slices; top each with about 1/3 cup salmon mixture. Top with remaining 4 bread slices. Yield: 4 servings (serving size: 1 sandwich).

notes: CALORIES 362; FAT 12.7g (sat 1.9g, mono 5.4g, poly 3.9g); PROTEIN 34g; CARB 29.4g; FIBER 0.3g; CHOL 74mg; IRON 2.9mg; SODIUM 850mg; CALC 87mg

recipes.title: Balsamic Pork with Shallots
recipes.servings_yield: 4 servings (serving size: 3 ounces pork and 1/4 cup shallot mixture)
recipes.description: This dish is reminiscent of bistro-style steak with shallot sauce. Serve with rice, egg noodles, or roasted potatoes.

ingredients.item: pork tenderloin, trimmed and cut crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick slices

instructions.text: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Sprinkle pork with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add pork to pan; cook 3 minutes on each side or until done. Remove from pan, and keep warm.

Add remaining 4 teaspoons oil to pan; reduce heat to medium. Add shallots to pan; cook 10 minutes or until tender, stirring occasionally. Add garlic; cook 2 minutes. Stir in 1/2 cup water and vinegar; simmer 6 minutes. Stir in remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and remaining 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Spoon shallot mixture over pork. Serve immediately. Yield: 4 servings (serving size: 3 ounces pork and 1/4 cup shallot mixture).

notes: CALORIES 260; FAT 9.4g (sat 2.1g, mono 5.9g, poly 1.1g); PROTEIN 26.2g; CARB 16.9g; FIBER 0.7g; CHOL 74mg; IRON 2.6mg; SODIUM 365mg; CALC 44mg

recipes.title: Paprika Pork
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Keeping It Simple
recipes.description: Assorted colors of fresh peppers and paprika turn bottled marinara into a rich Hungarian goulash-style sauce for a quick, hearty weeknight supper.

ingredients.item: pork tenderloin, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions.text: Heat a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray.
Add bell peppers to pan; sauté 5 minutes or until tender. Remove from pan; keep warm.
Cook pasta according to package directions, omitting salt and fat. Drain. Set aside.

Coat pan with cooking spray. Sprinkle pork with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper; add pork to pan; cook 4 minutes, browning on all sides. Add paprika; cook 1 minute. Add wine, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 25 minutes or until meat is tender, stirring occasionally. Stir in remaining salt and pepper; cook 1 minute. Serve over pasta. Yield: 4 servings (serving size: about 3/4 cup pork mixture and 3/4 cup noodles).

notes: CALORIES 296; FAT 5.5g (sat 2.2g, mono 2.5g, poly 0.4g); PROTEIN 25g; CARB 18.8g; FIBER 5.4g; CHOL 107mg; IRON 4.4mg; SODIUM 646mg; CALC 40mg

recipes.title: Sausage and Roasted Pepper Pasta
recipes.description: Four assertive ingredients—hot Italian sausage, roasted red peppers, and green peppers—fry into a simple, satisfying supper. Try it with a light red, and maybe some garlic bread, for a quick, nearly weeknight supper.

instructions.text: Preheat broiler.

Cut bell peppers in half lengthwise; discard seeds and membranes. Place pepper halves, skin sides up, on a foil-lined baking sheet; flatten with hand. Broil 10 minutes or until blackened. Place in a zip-top plastic bag; seal. Let stand 15 minutes. Peel and cut into strips.
Cook pasta with cooking spray. Sprinkle with salt.

recipes.title: Albondigas Soup

ingredients.item: bag frozen pepper stir-fry (such as Birds Eye)
boneless chicken breast, trimmed and cut into 3/4-inch pieces

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add pepper stir-fry to pan; sauté 5 minutes. Add carrots; sauté, stirring occasionally. Add broth, chiles, and tomatoes; bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 15 minutes or until carrots are tender, stirring occasionally.

Place one-third of broth mixture in blender (let allow steam to escape); process until smooth. Return to pan. Add remaining broth mixture; bring to a boil. Drop by rounded tablespoon into broth mixture. Add remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Stir in juice and remaining 1/4 cup cilantro. Serve immediately. Yield: 12 servings (serving size: about 1 1/3 cups).

notes: CALORIES 136; FAT 4.7g (sat 1.2g, mono 2.0g, poly 0.8g); PROTEIN 20.2g; CARB 4.2g; FIBER 0.8g; CHOL 59mg; IRON 1.4mg; SODIUM 796mg; CALC 29mg

recipes.title: Monday Morning Potato Rolls and Bread
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Reader Recipes by Catherine McMichael, Saginaw, Mich.
recipes.servings_yield: Yield: 18 servings (serving size: 1 roll or one-ninth of loaf)
recipes.description: I make a fairly traditional Sunday meal of chicken and potatoes for my family. I hated to see the leftovers go to waste, so I used the mashed potatoes to create these delicious rolls. I experimented with 10 variations before settling on this version. My kids and husband love the rolls so much that they never last until Tuesday!

ingredients.item: mashed cooked peeled baking potatoes (about 8 ounces)

instructions.text: Combine first 4 ingredients in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave at HIGH for 2 minutes or until mixture is 110°. Stir with a whisk until smooth.

Weigh or lightly spoon flour into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Combine 6.75 ounces (about 1 1/2 cups) flour, yeast, and salt in a large mixing bowl. Add potato mixture to flour mixture, stirring with a fork until combined. Add eggs; stir until combined.

Add 9 ounces (about 2 cups) flour to potato mixture; stir until a soft dough forms. Turn dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 10 minutes); add enough of remaining 1/2 cup flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, to prevent dough from sticking to hands (dough will feel sticky).

Place dough in a large bowl coated with olive oil, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If indentation remains, dough has risen enough.) Punch dough down; cover and let rest 5 minutes.

Divide dough in half. Working with one portion at a time (cover remaining dough to prevent drying), roll one portion into a 14 x 7-inch rectangle on a floured surface. Roll up rectangle tightly, starting with a short edge, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets; pinch seam and ends to seal. Place loaf, seam side down, in an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray.

Shape remaining portion into 9 portions, and shape each into a ball. Place balls in an 8-inch square baking dish coated with cooking spray. Coat top of loaf and rolls with cooking spray. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 30 minutes or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If the indentation remains, dough has risen enough.)
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until tops of rolls are browned and loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. Remove from pans; cool on wire racks.

notes: CALORIES 168; FAT 2.8g (sat 1.1g, mono 0.8g, poly 0.4g); PROTEIN 5.7g; CARB 30.1g; FIBER 1.1g; CHOL 28mg; IRON 1.8mg; SODIUM 207mg; CALC 24mg

recipes.title: Creamy Carrot Soup
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Category Finalist Starters and Drinks by Lisa Richardson, Glendale, Calif.
recipes.description: I prepared this soup for my parents, who watch my daughter one afternoon a week. They absolutely loved its velvety sweetness. Garnish with shredded carrot and fresh mint.

ingredients.item: chopped Vidalia or other sweet onion

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and carrots to pan; cook 10 minutes, stirring frequently. Stir in salt, pepper, and ginger.
Add 2 cups water and broth to pan; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 25 minutes or until carrots are tender. Remove from heat; cool.

Place half of carrot mixture and 1 tablespoon cream in a food processor or blender; process 20 seconds or until smooth. Pour pureed mixture into a large bowl. Repeat procedure with remaining carrot mixture and 1 tablespoon cream. Return mixture to pan; cook over medium heat until thoroughly heated. Yield: 4 servings (serving size: 1 1/2 cups).

notes: CALORIES 180; FAT 6.9g (sat 2.3g, mono 3.3g, poly 0.9g); PROTEIN 3.5g; CARB 28.7g; FIBER 7.6g; CHOL 10mg; IRON 0.9mg; SODIUM 963mg; CALC 97mg

recipes.title: Swanson Pan Sautéed Chicken with Vegetables and Herbs

ingredients.item: fresh whole baby carrots (about 16), green tops trimmed to 1 inch

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Combine black pepper, paprika and flour. Coat the chicken with flour mixture.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until it's well browned on all sides. Remove the chicken from the skillet.
Add the onions and potatoes to the skillet and cook for 5 minutes. Add the carrots, stock, lemon juice and oregano and heat to a boil. Return the chicken to the skillet. Cover the skillet.
Bake at 350°F. for 20 minutes. Uncover the skillet and bake for 15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender. Sprinkle with the thyme.

recipes.title: Deep Dark Chocolate Biscotti
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Reader Recipes by Linda Rogers, Manistee, Mich.
recipes.description: Whole-wheat flour, flaxseed, and almonds add fiber and antioxidants.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°.

Weigh or lightly spoon flour into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Combine flour, flaxseed, soda, and salt in a bowl, stirring with a whisk. Combine sugars, egg whites, and egg in a bowl; beat with a mixer at high speed for 2 minutes. Add vanilla; mix well. Add flour mixture to egg mixture; stir until combined. Fold in chocolate and almonds. Divide dough into 3 equal portions. Roll each portion into a 6-inch-long roll. Arrange rolls 3 inches apart on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Pat to a 1-inch thickness. Bake at 350° for 28 minutes or until firm.

Remove rolls from baking sheet; cool 10 minutes on a wire rack. Cut rolls diagonally into 30 (1/2-inch) slices. Place, cut sides down, on baking sheet. Reduce oven temperature to 325°; bake 7 minutes. Turn cookies over; bake 7 minutes (cookies will be slightly soft in center but will harden as they cool). Remove from baking sheet; cool on wire rack. Yield: 2 1/2 dozen (serving size: 1 biscotto).

notes: CALORIES 94; FAT 2.7g (sat 0.8g, mono 1.1g, poly 0.7g); PROTEIN 2.7g; CARB 14.4g; FIBER 1.1g; CHOL 7mg; IRON 0.9mg; SODIUM 49mg; CALC 18mg

recipes.title: Broccoli and Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine - Lighten Up by Kathy Kitchens Downie, RD
recipes.description: If the broccoli florets are large, break into smaller pieces at the stalk instead of chopping them; they'll cook more quickly. Count on having dinner on the table in about 40 minutes, and serve this soup the moment it's done for the best results. In fact, if you wait, you'll find it gets thicker with time. If you have leftovers, you will want to thin the soup with a little chicken broth or milk to the desired consistency.

ingredients.item: shredded light processed cheese (such as Velveeta Light)

instructions.text: Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray. Add onion, mushrooms, and garlic to pan; sauté 5 minutes or until liquid evaporates, stirring occasionally. Reduce heat to medium; add butter to mushroom mixture, stirring until butter melts. Sprinkle mushroom mixture with flour; cook 2 minutes, stirring occasionally. Gradually add milk and broth, stirring constantly with a whisk; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low; cook 10 minutes or until slightly thick, stirring constantly.

Add pasta to pan; cook 10 minutes. Add cheese to pan, and stir until cheese melts. Add chicken and remaining ingredients to pan; cook 5 minutes or until broccoli is tender and soup is thoroughly heated. Yield: 10 servings (serving size: 1 cup).

notes: Before: CALORIES 534, FAT 33g, SODIUM 1,289mg | After: CALORIES 317; FAT 12.3g (sat 6.8g, mono 2.9g, poly 0.9g); PROTEIN 27.5g; CARB 23.8g; FIBER 1.9g; CHOL 74mg; IRON 1.6mg; SODIUM 723mg; CALC 179mg

recipes.title: Bucatini alla Carbonara
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine March 2009 - Cooking Class
recipes.description: Ragù alla Bolognese sauces are popular throughout Italy. The most prominent, originating in the northern city of Bologna. Even among residents of the city in which it hails, different variations abound. Guanciale (GWAHN-CHAY-lay) is cured pork jowl.

instructions.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add guanciale; cook until crisp, stirring frequently. Remove from heat; set aside from the pan.

Bring 6 quarts water and salt to a boil. Add pasta to pot. Cook 1 minute or until almost al dente, tossing constantly. (Do not overcook. Stir sauce and chicken and pasta is al dente.) Cook 5 minutes or until thick, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Add pancetta and pasta to guanciale. Place about 1 cup pasta mixture on each of 6 plates; sprinkle each serving with 2 teaspoons remaining cheese. Yield: 6 servings.

notes: CALORIES 389; FAT 16.4g (sat 5.8g, mono 6.5g, poly 1.4g); PROTEIN 17.6g; CARB 42g; FIBER 1.6g; CHOL 130mg; IRON 2.5mg; SODIUM 522mg; CALC 106mg

recipes.title: Fettuccine with Olive Oil, Garlic, and Red Pepper
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine March 2009 - Cooking Class

instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic; cook 30 seconds or until fragrant, stirring occasionally. Do not brown. Add pasta, remaining salt.

Combine 1/4 cup cheese, and remaining 2 tablespoons oil, stirring well. Add egg mixture to pasta mixture; toss constantly to combine. Place pasta mixture on each of 6 plates. Cover, return water to a boil. Uncover and cook 8 minutes or until almost al dente. Drain pasta in a colander over a bowl, reserving 1 cup cooking water. Add pasta, reserved cup of cooking water. Add fat to a boil in an 8-quart pot. Add pasta to pot. Stir. Cover; return water to a boil.

Add remaining 4 teaspoons oil to pan; garlic mixture; heat medium-high; toss 2 minutes or until pasta is al dente, tossing to combine or until pasta is heated through. Place 1 cup mixture on each of 6 plates; sprinkle each serving with 1 teaspoon remaining cheese; drizzle each with 1 teaspoon remaining oil. Yield: 6 servings.

notes: CALORIES 352; FAT 10.2g (sat 1.8g, mono 6.6g, poly 1.1g); PROTEIN 9.7g; CARB 54.1g; FIBER 2.6g; CHOL 0mg; IRON 3mg; SODIUM 423mg; CALC 27mg

recipes.title: Tagliatelle alla Bolognese
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine March 2009 - Cooking Class
recipes.servings_yield: 6 servings (serving size: about 1/4 cup sauce over shallow bowl, spoon about 3/4 cup sauce over each serving)
recipes.description: Meat-based pasta sauces are popular throughout Italy. The most prominent, ragù alla Bolognese, originated in the northern city of Bologna. Even among residents of the city in which it hails, different variations abound.

instructions.text: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-heat. Add pancetta to pan, and cook 2 minutes. Add chopped onion, chopped celery, and chopped carrot; cook 10 minutes or until tender, stirring occasionally. Add ground veal, ground pork, 1 teaspoon salt, and pepper; cook 5 minutes or until browned, stirring to crumble. Stir in wine. Cook 3 minutes or until liquid almost evaporates, stirring occasionally. Reduce heat to medium-low.

Stir in tomato paste, stirring occasionally until almost evaporates. Place parsley sprigs and next 3 ingredients (through thyme) on a double layer of cheesecloth. Gather edges of cheesecloth together; tie securely. Add cheesecloth bag and milk to pan; bring to a simmer. Simmer on low heat 1 hour or until thick, stirring occasionally. Discard cheesecloth bag.

Bring 4 quarts water and remaining 1 tablespoon salt to a boil in an 8-quart pot. Add pasta to pot. Stir. Cover; return water to a boil. Uncover and cook 8 minutes or until al dente. Drain. Place 1 cup pasta in each of 6 shallow bowls. Spoon about 3/4 cup sauce over each serving. Sprinkle each with 1 tablespoon chopped parsley. Yield: 6 servings.

notes: CALORIES 555; FAT 17.2g (sat 6.9g, mono 6.8g, poly 1.3g); PROTEIN 27.5g; CARB 63.5g; FIBER 3.4g; CHOL 107mg; IRON 3.4mg; SODIUM 597mg; CALC 88mg

Wine note: A pasta with Bolognese sauce needs a wine that will balance the richness of the pork, veal, and pancetta plus mirror the acidity of the tomato paste. A wine made from sangiovese grapes—such as Chianti—is gorgeous specifically for a Chianti Classico, which is richer and earthier than basic. A great wine for the price is the Chianti Classico 2005 ($14). —Karen MacNeil

recipes.title: How to Make Fresh Tomato Sauce
recipes.source_note: Cooking Light Magazine March 2009 - Cooking Class
recipes.description: Fresh tomato sauce is a staple in Italy, where it's usually served with spaghetti. Although the sauce tastes rich and delicious, it only takes about 30 minutes to prepare. See recipe on page 138.

instructions.text: To peel tomatoes, core and cut a small X through the skin on the bottom of tomatoes with a sharp knife. Place them in boiling water for about 30 seconds or just until skins begin to peel back. Quickly remove tomatoes from pan, and plunge them into ice water. Drain and remove skins. Cut each tomato in half lengthwise, and squeeze the juices and seeds into a colander over a bowl. Reserve tomato juices, and discard seeds. Finely chop tomatoes.
Heat extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic, and cook just until it begins to brown lightly, taking care not to burn it.
Add tomatoes and reserved juices, and cook until almost all of the liquid evaporates.

Finish cooking the pasta with the sauce, which should be in a skillet large enough to combine the two and allow for tossing. Add enough of the pasta cooking water to the sauce to give the dish a creamy texture and marry the sauce to the pasta.
