When tender, take away the gravy and thicken with flour and butter, and boil, brown the round with butter and flour, adding ketchup and wine to your taste.

notes: Original 1796 recipe
Alamode = braised/pot roasted

recipes.title: Currant Jelly
recipes.description: Colonial currant jelly preserved with brandy-dipped paper.

instructions.text: Having stripped the currants from the stalks, put them in a stone jar, stop it close, set it in a kettle of boiling water, half way the jar.
Let it boil half an hour, take it out and (strain the juice through a coarse hair sieve, to a pint of juice put a pound of sugar.
Set it over a fine quick fire in a preserving pan, or a bell-metal skillet, keep stirring it all the time till the sugar be melted, then skim the skum off as fast as it rises.

When the jelly is very clear and fine, pour it into earthen or china cups, when cold, cut white papers just the bigness of the top of the pot, and lay on the jelly, dip those papers in brandy, then cover the top of the pot and prick it full of holes.
Set it in a dry place; you may put some into glasses for present use.

notes: Original 1796 recipe
Cover with brandy-dipped paper to preserve

recipes.title: To Keep Green Peas till Christmas
recipes.description: Colonial method for preserving green peas through winter using mutton suet.

instructions.text: Take young peas, shell them, put them in a cullender to drain.
Then lay a cloth four or five times double on a table, then spread them on, dry them very well.
Have your bottles ready, fill them, cover them with mutton suet fat when it is a little soft.
Fill the necks almost to the top, cork them, tie a bladder and a leather over them and set them in a dry cool place.

notes: Original 1796 recipe
Colonial preservation method for winter storage

recipes.title: To Boil Asparagus
recipes.description: Colonial method for preparing asparagus with toast and butter.

ingredients.prep_note: cut into small pieces, for garnish

instructions.text: Scrape asparagus, cut them even lengths and tie them in small bundles.
Put them into boiling water with salt in it.
When tender, take them up carefully, dip the toast in the asparagus water.
Lay it in the bottom of your dish; then lay the heads of the asparagus on it, with the white ends outwards.
Pour a little melted butter over the heads; cut an orange into small pieces, and stick them between for garnish.

notes: Original 1796 recipe

recipes.title: Onion-Soup-Based Swedish Meatball Sauce
recipes.source_note: Family recipe card with handwritten modifications
recipes.description: A creamy Swedish meatball sauce using mushroom gravy and onion soup mixes. Handwritten notes suggest adjustments for larger batches.

ingredients.prep_note: or 3 cans mushroom soup per handwritten note
or 1 can water per handwritten note

instructions.text: Combine gravy and soup mixes and water.
Bring to a boil stirring constantly.
Simmer for one minute.
Reduce heat to low, and add sour cream.

notes: Handwritten annotations suggest variations: use 3 cans mushroom soup, 3 packages onion soup mix, 1 can water, and 1/2 container sour cream for a different proportion.

recipes.title: Watermelon Smoothie
recipes.description: A refreshing watermelon smoothie with milk, vanilla yogurt, and maple syrup.

instructions.text: Put in blender all together.
Mix until smooth.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Ghost Pepper Hot Sauce
recipes.description: A slow-cooker method for making ghost pepper hot sauce with brown sugar, molasses, and vegetables for a complex, fiery condiment.

ingredients.prep_note: stems removed, seeds optional (remove for less heat)

instructions.text: SAFETY FIRST: Wear nitrile gloves when handling ghost peppers. Work in a well-ventilated area. Avoid touching your face.
Remove stems from ghost peppers. Remove seeds if you want less heat (seeds and membrane contain the most capsaicin).
Add all ingredients to the slow cooker: peppers, brown sugar, molasses (if using), ketchup, mustard, vinegar, water, carrots, garlic, and salt.
Cook on low until mixture reaches 180°F, about 1-2 hours. The carrots should be soft.
Transfer contents to a blender or food processor. Blend until completely smooth.
If using xanthan gum for thickening, add it while blending and process for another 30 seconds.
Taste carefully (it's HOT!) and adjust salt and sugar as needed.
For bottling: Sterilize bottles by boiling in water for 10 minutes. Pour hot sauce into hot bottles, leaving 1/4 inch headspace. Seal immediately.
Store in refrigerator for up to 6 months. Flavors will develop and meld over 1-2 weeks.

notes: Ghost peppers are EXTREMELY hot - one of the hottest peppers in the world. Use caution.
The carrots add natural sweetness and help cut the heat slightly.
Molasses gives a deeper, more complex flavor profile.
Xanthan gum helps the sauce cling to food better but is optional.
Flavors improve with age - wait at least a week before using for best results.

recipes.title: Ghost Pepper Hot Sauce (Stovetop)
recipes.description: Make your own ghost pepper hot sauce at home with plenty of chopped ghost peppers, tomatoes, vinegar and salt. Big flavor, big spice with a pleasant blast of heat. Drizzle it over everything!

instructions.text: Heat oil in a pan and add peppers and onions. Stir.
Add tomatoes and stir. Cook about 10 minutes.
Add vinegar, salt and water. Simmer 20 minutes to allow flavors to develop.
Transfer contents to a food processor and process until smooth.
Transfer to a container. Seal and refrigerate until ready to use.

notes: The flavors will grow more intense the longer you wait.
Heat Level: VERY HOT. Ghost peppers are one of the hottest chili peppers in the world, so beware.
Makes about 2 cups of hot sauce.

assumptions: Based on 20 servings from about 2 cups total

recipes.title: Habanero Hot Sauce
recipes.description: The perfect mix of fire and flavor with Caribbean red habaneros, carrot, shallot, garlic, and a blend of spices.

instructions.text: Add all ingredients (carrots, shallots, habaneros, garlic, vinegar, spices) to a small pot or sauce pan and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 10-15 minutes, or until all ingredients are softened.
Transfer to a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
Taste and adjust for salt and spices. For thinner consistency, add water 1 tablespoon at a time.
Bottle and serve. Better after 1-2 days to let flavors mingle.

notes: Strain for thinner consistency or add more vinegar to thin out.
Use apple cider vinegar for tangier flavor.
Habaneros range 100,000-350,000 Scoville Heat Units - very hot!

recipes.title: Classic Chili
recipes.description: Loaded with ground beef, fire roasted tomatoes, beans, and perfect seasonings - thick, chunky, and easy to make.

ingredients.prep_note: diced, or use bell peppers for milder

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and peppers, cook 2-3 minutes to soften.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add ground beef and break apart with wooden spoon. Cook until browned.
Add tomato paste, fire roasted tomatoes, crushed tomatoes, and beef broth. Stir to combine.
Add chili powder, cumin, cayenne (if using), salt and pepper.
Add beans and stir well.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasonings. Serve with your favorite toppings.

notes: Can use chuck roast or brisket cooked low and slow for amazing results.
Mix kidney beans with black beans or pinto beans for variety.
Use a mix of chili powders: ancho, guajillo, chipotle for complex flavor.

recipes.title: Restaurant-Style Salsa
recipes.description: Classic restaurant-style salsa with juicy tomatoes, jalapeño, onion, lime and a special ingredient.

instructions.text: Add all ingredients to a food processor or blender.
Pulse until you reach your preferred consistency - best when still a bit chunky.
Taste and adjust salt and lime as needed.
Transfer to a bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let flavors meld.

notes: Use fire-roasted tomatoes for smoky flavor.
Add more jalapeños or serrano peppers for extra heat.
Keeps refrigerated for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Jalapeño Hot Sauce
recipes.description: Bright and citrusy jalapeño hot sauce with fresh jalapeños and lime juice, perfect for drizzling over everything.

instructions.text: Add jalapeños, lime juice, vinegar, garlic, and salt to a blender.
Blend until smooth, adding water as needed for desired consistency.
Taste and adjust salt and lime.
Transfer to a bottle and refrigerate.

notes: No cooking required - fresh and bright flavor.
Made with only 6 ingredients.
Great on tacos, nachos, eggs, and more.

recipes.title: Texas Chili
recipes.description: Bold and authentic Texas Chili with tender beef chuck and rich chili paste - no beans, the perfect hearty meal.

instructions.text: Toast dried chiles in a dry skillet for 1-2 minutes. Soak in hot water for 20 minutes.
Blend soaked chiles with 1 cup beef broth until smooth to make chili paste.
Season beef with salt. Brown in batches in oil in a large pot. Set aside.
Sauté onion until soft, add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add chili paste, remaining broth, cumin, and oregano. Stir well.
Return beef to pot. Bring to boil, reduce heat, and simmer 2+ hours until beef is tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve.

notes: Texas chili traditionally has NO beans.
The longer you simmer, the more tender the beef.
Serve with cornbread, crackers, or over rice.

recipes.title: Classic Stuffed Peppers
recipes.description: The quintessential stuffed bell peppers with seasoned ground beef, rice, and melty cheese.

ingredients.prep_note: any color, tops removed and seeded

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brown ground beef with onion and garlic in a large skillet. Drain excess fat.
Stir in cooked rice, half the tomato sauce, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.
Stuff peppers with beef mixture and place in baking dish.
Pour remaining tomato sauce over peppers.
Cover with foil and bake 35 minutes.
Remove foil, top with cheese, and bake 10 more minutes until cheese melts.

notes: Use any color bell pepper - green, yellow, red, or orange.
Can substitute ground turkey or Italian sausage.
Add jalapeño to filling for extra heat.

recipes.title: Pepper Jelly
recipes.description: A simple, super addictive jam that makes it to the recipe box of best all-time recipes. A no-worry recipe.

instructions.text: Combine peppers, vinegar, and sugar in a large pot.
Bring to a rolling boil, stirring constantly.
Stir in pectin and return to boil for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and skim off any foam.
Ladle into sterilized jars, leaving 1/4 inch headspace.
Process in boiling water bath for 10 minutes or refrigerate.

notes: Perfect over cream cheese with crackers.
Great as a glaze for grilled meats.
Add more jalapeños for spicier jelly.

recipes.title: Pickled Jalapeños
recipes.description: The best crunchy, spicy pickled jalapeños with a touch of sweet, ready in only 10 minutes.

instructions.text: Pack sliced jalapeños into a clean jar.
Combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to boil.
Pour hot brine over jalapeños, making sure they're fully covered.
Let cool, then seal and refrigerate.
Best after 24 hours. Keeps for several weeks refrigerated.

notes: Add garlic cloves for extra flavor.
Leave seeds in for more heat.
Perfect for tacos, nachos, sandwiches.

recipes.title: Homemade Cajun Seasoning
recipes.description: The perfect blend of everyday spices to add flavor and zing to meats, seafood, soups, stews, and gumbos.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
Transfer to an airtight container.
Store in a cool, dark place for up to 6 months.

notes: Adjust cayenne for more or less heat.
Great on chicken, shrimp, fish, and vegetables.
Use for gumbo, jambalaya, and blackened dishes.

recipes.title: Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.description: Authentic Sichuan style wok-fried chicken in sweet, savory, and spicy sauce with peanuts and dried chilies. Ready in 10 minutes.

instructions.text: Mix soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, and cornstarch for sauce. Set aside.
Heat oil in wok over high heat until smoking.
Add dried chilies and stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, cook 30 seconds.
Pour in sauce and toss to coat.
Add peanuts and green onions. Serve immediately over rice.

notes: Use Sichuan peppercorns for authentic flavor.
Dried chilies add flavor, not just heat.
Can substitute with chicken thighs for juicier meat.

recipes.title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
recipes.description: Loaded with Caribbean flavor, marinated in spicy Scotch bonnet sauce, perfect for grilling or baking.

instructions.text: Blend all marinade ingredients (peppers through nutmeg) until smooth.
Score chicken pieces and coat thoroughly with marinade.
Marinate at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Grill over medium heat for 35-40 minutes, turning occasionally.
Or bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F.

notes: Scotch bonnets are very hot - use gloves when handling.
Can substitute habaneros if Scotch bonnets unavailable.
Traditional jerk is cooked over pimento wood.

recipes.title: Birria Tacos
recipes.description: Tender shredded beef simmered in chili sauce on lightly fried tortillas, served with consommé for dipping.

instructions.text: Toast dried chiles in dry skillet. Cover with hot water and soak 20 minutes.
Blend soaked chiles with tomatoes, onion, garlic, spices, and 1 cup broth until smooth.
Season beef chunks with salt. Brown in a large pot in batches.
Add chili sauce and remaining broth to pot. Bring to boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 2.5-3 hours until beef is fall-apart tender.
Remove beef and shred. Reserve cooking liquid (consommé).
Dip tortillas in consommé, then fry in skillet. Add cheese and shredded beef.
Fold and crisp on both sides. Serve with consommé for dipping, cilantro, and onion.

notes: The consommé is key - don't skip the dipping!
Can make in slow cooker on low for 8 hours.
For quesabirria, add extra cheese and fold tortilla in half.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.description: Popular North African and Middle Eastern dish of eggs poached in spicy tomato sauce, perfect for breakfast or any time.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté onion and bell pepper until soft.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, cumin, paprika, cayenne, and salt. Simmer 10 minutes.
Make 6 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook 8-10 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks are still runny.
Garnish with herbs and feta. Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

notes: The runny yolk mixed with sauce is the best part.
Add harissa for more heat and authentic flavor.
Serve straight from the skillet.

recipes.title: Pad Thai
recipes.description: Restaurant quality Pad Thai with chewy rice noodles, shrimp, scrambled eggs and vegetables in flavorful sauce. Done in 30 minutes.

instructions.text: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable. Drain.
Mix fish sauce, tamarind, brown sugar, and vinegar for sauce.
Heat oil in wok over high heat. Cook shrimp until pink, set aside.
Add more oil, scramble eggs, and set aside.
Add garlic, cook 30 seconds. Add noodles and sauce, toss to coat.
Add shrimp, eggs, half the bean sprouts and green onions. Toss together.
Serve topped with remaining sprouts, peanuts, and lime wedges.

notes: Use tamarind paste, not concentrate - dilute if needed.
Can substitute chicken or tofu for shrimp.
Work quickly - high heat is key.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Dip
recipes.description: Rich, cheesy, and spicy dip made with three cheeses, tender chicken, and Buffalo sauce. Includes slow cooker and oven directions.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix cream cheese, Buffalo sauce, and ranch in a bowl until smooth.
Fold in shredded chicken and half the cheddar.
Transfer to baking dish and top with remaining cheeses.
Bake 20 minutes until bubbly and golden.
Garnish with green onions. Serve with celery, chips, or bread.

notes: For slow cooker: combine all, cook low 2-3 hours, stir occasionally.
Use rotisserie chicken for easy prep.
Adjust Buffalo sauce for desired heat level.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.description: Indian-style curry with yogurt-marinated chicken roasted and simmered in creamy tomato-based curry sauce.

instructions.text: Mix yogurt, 1 tbsp garam masala, cumin, turmeric, and salt. Marinate chicken 1+ hours.
Roast marinated chicken at 425°F for 15-20 minutes until charred edges.
Melt butter in pan. Sauté onion until soft. Add garlic and ginger.
Add remaining garam masala, paprika. Cook 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in cream and roasted chicken. Simmer 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro. Serve over basmati rice with naan.

notes: Longer marinating = more flavorful chicken.
Can use coconut cream for dairy-free version.
Traditional tikka is cooked in tandoor oven.

recipes.title: Chili Oil Noodles
recipes.description: Satisfying noodles tossed with garlic, chilies, scallions, and cilantro in spicy hot oil.

instructions.text: Cook noodles according to package. Drain and place in serving bowls.
Place pepper flakes and garlic in a heatproof bowl.
Heat vegetable oil until shimmering. Carefully pour over pepper flakes (it will sizzle).
Add soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar to the chili oil. Mix well.
Pour chili oil mixture over noodles. Toss to coat.
Top with green onions and cilantro. Serve immediately.

notes: Works with any type of noodles.
Add a fried egg on top for extra protein.
Adjust chili flakes for desired heat.

recipes.title: Seafood Gumbo
recipes.description: Flavorful Louisiana gumbo with shrimp, white fish, crab, and oysters with plenty of Cajun seasonings.

instructions.text: Make roux: heat oil, whisk in flour, cook stirring constantly until dark brown (20-30 min).
Add onion, celery, bell pepper (the 'trinity'). Cook 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in stock. Add Cajun seasoning, bay leaves, and sausage.
Simmer 30 minutes.
Add fish and cook 10 minutes.
Add shrimp, crab, and oysters. Cook until shrimp are pink, about 5 minutes.
Remove bay leaves. Serve over rice with hot sauce.

notes: The roux is critical - don't burn it or you'll have to start over.
File powder thickens and adds earthy flavor - add off heat.
Okra also helps thicken traditionally.

recipes.title: Homemade Buffalo Sauce
recipes.description: Buttery, tangy, spicy homemade Buffalo sauce that's better than store-bought, perfect for wings, chicken, dips, pizza, and more.

instructions.text: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in hot sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire, and spices.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes, whisking constantly.
Remove from heat. Use immediately or store refrigerated.

notes: Add ghost pepper flakes for extreme heat.
Use for wings, dips, sandwiches, pizza, and more.
Keeps refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Crispy Buffalo Wings
recipes.description: Crispy on the outside, juicy inside, drenched in fiery buttery Buffalo sauce. The ultimate bar-style wings experience.

instructions.text: Pat wings completely dry with paper towels - this is key for crispy skin.
Toss wings with baking powder, salt, and garlic powder.
Arrange on wire rack over baking sheet.
Bake at 425°F for 45-50 minutes, flipping halfway, until crispy.
Toss hot wings with Buffalo sauce. Serve with ranch or blue cheese.

notes: Baking powder helps create extra crispy skin.
Pat wings as dry as possible for best results.
Recipe originated at Anchor Bar in Buffalo, NY.

recipes.title: Bacon Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.description: Spicy jalapeño poppers filled with seasoned cream cheese and cheddar, wrapped in smoky bacon and baked to crispy perfection.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Mix cream cheese, cheddar, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Fill each jalapeño half with cheese mixture.
Wrap each popper with half slice of bacon, securing with toothpick.
Arrange on baking sheet. Bake 20-25 minutes until bacon is crispy.

notes: Wear gloves when handling jalapeños.
Can be grilled instead of baked.
Remove seeds for less heat.

recipes.title: Chicken Vindaloo
recipes.description: Fiery and tangy Indian curry from Goa with chicken marinated in spiced vinegar-based sauce. One of the spiciest curries.

instructions.text: Blend soaked chilies, vinegar, garlic, ginger, and spices into paste.
Coat chicken in paste. Marinate at least 1 hour, preferably overnight.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds until they pop. Add onion and cook until soft.
Add marinated chicken and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes and enough water to create sauce. Simmer 30-40 minutes.
Adjust seasoning. Serve over basmati rice.

notes: Name comes from Portuguese 'carne de vinha d'alhos' - meat in wine vinegar and garlic.
One of the hottest Indian curries - adjust chilies to preference.
Keeps 5 days refrigerated.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
recipes.description: Popular creamy Indian curry with rich buttery gravy and warming spices. Incredibly easy to make and not spicy hot.

instructions.text: Mix yogurt, half the garam masala, and turmeric. Marinate chicken 30+ minutes.
Cook marinated chicken in butter until lightly browned. Set aside.
In same pan, add more butter. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger.
Add remaining garam masala and tomato puree. Simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in cream and return chicken to pan. Simmer 10-15 minutes.
Add kasuri methi if using. Serve with naan and basmati rice.

notes: Mild curry - great for those who love flavor but not heat.
Garam masala and turmeric are essential.
Marinate overnight for deeper flavor.

recipes.title: Lamb Korma
recipes.description: Comforting Indian curry with tender lamb simmered in creamy cashew-yogurt sauce until super tender. Includes slow cooker method.

instructions.text: Pulse cashews in food processor. Add tomato paste, garlic, ginger, spices to form paste.
Mix paste with yogurt. Coat lamb and marinate 1+ hours.
Brown marinated lamb in oil. Set aside.
Sauté onion until golden. Return lamb with marinade.
Add water to cover. Simmer 60 minutes until lamb is tender.
Stir in cream. Adjust seasoning and serve.

notes: For slow cooker: cook on low 6-8 hours.
The cashew paste creates incredibly creamy sauce.
Can use chicken or beef instead of lamb.

recipes.title: Shrimp Tacos with Creamy Jalapeño Sauce
recipes.description: Spiced shrimp on warm tortillas with crunchy Fresno chili slaw and creamy jalapeño sauce (salsa doña style).

instructions.text: Season shrimp with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Blend mayo, jalapeño, cilantro, and lime juice for creamy sauce.
Toss cabbage with Fresno chili and lime juice for slaw.
Cook shrimp in oil 2-3 minutes per side until pink.
Warm tortillas. Fill with slaw, shrimp, and drizzle with sauce.

notes: The creamy jalapeño sauce makes the dish.
Can grill the shrimp for smoky flavor.
Add avocado for extra creaminess.

recipes.title: Fish Tacos
recipes.description: Seasoned pan-seared white fish with crunchy slaw, avocado, and creamy homemade fish taco sauce.

instructions.text: Season fish with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, white pepper, and salt.
Make slaw: toss cabbage, jalapeño, cilantro, lime, and honey.
Pan-sear fish in oil 3-4 minutes per side until flaky.
Break fish into chunks.
Warm tortillas. Layer slaw, fish, avocado, and sauce.

notes: Use any mild white fish - snapper, cod, tilapia, or mahi-mahi.
The roasted jalapeño in the slaw adds nice smoky heat.
Serve with extra lime wedges.

recipes.title: Chimichurri
recipes.description: Timeless Argentinian sauce made with oil, garlic and fresh herbs - perfect as sauce or marinade for grilled meats and seafood.

instructions.text: Combine parsley, oregano, and garlic in a bowl.
Whisk in vinegar, then slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking.
Add red pepper flakes and salt. Mix well.
Let sit 10-15 minutes for flavors to meld. Best after 30 minutes.

notes: A very personal recipe - adjust herbs to taste.
Perfect with grilled steak, especially skirt or flank.
Can add cilantro for a twist.

recipes.title: Cuban Mojo Marinade
recipes.description: Traditional Cuban sauce with garlic, sour orange, olive oil and herbs - great for marinating fish, chicken, or pork, or as a garlicky sauce.

ingredients.prep_note: or 1/4 cup each orange and lime juice

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant but not browned, about 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Whisk in citrus juice, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Let cool. Use as marinade or sauce.

notes: Sour orange (naranja agria) is traditional but can substitute with regular citrus mix.
Essential components: garlic, sour orange juice, oregano, salt.
Marinate seafood 1 hour, pork 4-6 hours, overnight for deeper flavor.

recipes.title: Candied Bacon Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.description: Jalapeños stuffed with honey-sweetened ghost pepper cream cheese, wrapped in candied bacon. Sweet and spicy perfection.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Mix cream cheese, 2 tbsp honey, ghost pepper flakes, and garlic powder.
Fill each jalapeño half with cheese mixture.
Mix brown sugar and remaining honey. Rub over bacon slices.
Wrap each popper with candied bacon. Secure with toothpicks.
Bake 25-30 minutes until bacon is caramelized and crispy.

notes: The sweet-spicy combination is addictive.
Ghost pepper flakes add serious heat - adjust to preference.
Can smoke these for extra flavor.

recipes.title: Hot Honey Wings
recipes.description: Crispy baked chicken wings glazed with spicy hot honey - the perfect balance of sweet heat.

instructions.text: Pat wings dry. Toss with baking powder, salt, and pepper.
Arrange on wire rack over baking sheet.
Bake at 425°F for 45 minutes, flipping halfway.
Whisk honey, hot sauce, cayenne, and melted butter for glaze.
Toss hot wings with hot honey glaze. Serve immediately.

notes: The sweet-heat combo is incredibly addictive.
Can make your own hot honey by infusing honey with chili flakes.
Serve with blue cheese or ranch for dipping.

recipes.title: Classic Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.description: The original crispy fried jalapeño poppers stuffed with cream cheese and coated in seasoned breading.

instructions.text: Mix cream cheese, cheddar, and garlic powder.
Fill each jalapeño half with cheese mixture.
Set up breading station: flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs.
Dredge each popper in flour, dip in egg, coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F. Fry poppers 2-3 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with ranch.

notes: Can also bake at 400°F for 20 minutes.
Double-breading makes them extra crispy.
Perfect for game day or parties.

recipes.title: Homemade Taco Seasoning
recipes.description: Homemade taco seasoning loaded with chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic, onion and more - better than store-bought packets.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
Store in an airtight container.
Use 2 tablespoons per 1 lb of meat.

notes: Use for tacos, burritos, nachos, taco salads, and more.
No fillers or preservatives like store-bought.
Adjust cayenne for desired heat level.

recipes.title: Smoked Ghost Pepper Hot Sauce
recipes.description: Intensely spicy hot sauce made from dried, smoked ghost peppers with roasted garlic and vinegar. The smokiness makes this the most flavorful hot sauce.

instructions.text: Dry fresh, ripe ghost peppers by tying string to stems and hanging in pantry for approximately one month until completely dried. Ensure peppers don't touch for air circulation.
Smoke dried peppers on a smoker for 10-20 minutes, monitoring to prevent over-charring.
For roasted garlic: cut tops off heads, place in baking dish, drizzle with olive oil, cover with foil, bake at 375°F for 1 hour until soft and caramelized.
Remove seeds and stems from smoked peppers (wear gloves!). Discard any with mold.
Puree all ingredients in a powerful blender (Vitamix recommended) until smooth.
Heat sauce in large pot on medium heat with proper ventilation, reducing to about 80% original volume.
Strain through fine sieve.
Funnel into sterilized jars.

notes: Ghost peppers reach over 1 million Scoville Heat Units - use extreme caution.
Store unopened at room temperature; refrigerate after opening.
For shelf-stable storage: heat bottles in boiling water, fill with sauce at 180°F+, flip upside down 5 minutes.
Sauce will separate - shake before use.

recipes.title: Hot Carolina Reaper or Ghost Pepper Salt
recipes.description: Homemade spicy salt blend combining super-hot peppers with aromatic varieties. Customizable proportions work well with fresh or frozen peppers.

ingredients.prep_note: about 6 peppers - Carolina reapers, scorpion, or ghost peppers
about 6 peppers - habanero, scotch bonnet, or fatalii

instructions.text: Wearing gloves, remove stems from all peppers.
Cut peppers into pieces directly into a food processor.
Add salt and puree until finely ground with no large particles or skin pieces.
Spread mixture on parchment-lined baking sheet.
Air-dry 1-2 days until no longer wet. Fans accelerate drying.
Alternative: use dehydrator at 90°F for approximately 12 hours.
Store in labeled container in refrigerator for long-term storage.

notes: Use proportions as a template - customize to taste.
Works well with frozen peppers.
Drying releases strong aromas - consider drying in garage if using dehydrator.
Super-hot peppers add heat while aromatic peppers add fruity flavor.

recipes.title: Nacho Cheese Sauce
recipes.description: Spicy homemade nacho cheese sauce that tastes just like movie theater nachos, using a trick learned behind the concession stand.

instructions.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute to form roux.
Slowly whisk in milk until smooth.
Add cheese and stir until melted.
Stir in jalapeño brine, salt, and cayenne if using.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

notes: The jalapeño brine is the movie theater secret.
Can use American cheese for smoother consistency.
Add more cayenne for extra heat.

recipes.title: Texas Nachos
recipes.description: The ultimate appetizer with crispy corn tortillas topped with refried beans, melty cheese and pickled jalapeño peppers. Perfect for parties or game day!

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Spread tortilla chips on large baking sheet.
Warm refried beans and dollop over chips.
Top with shredded cheese and jalapeños.
Bake 10-15 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Add sour cream, guacamole, and salsa. Serve immediately.

notes: Layer chips in a single layer for best results.
Add seasoned ground beef for loaded nachos.
Serve immediately - don't let them sit or chips get soggy.

recipes.title: Quick and Easy Enchilada Sauce
recipes.description: Very flavorful quick and easy enchilada sauce ready in only 10 minutes. So much better than canned sauce.

instructions.text: Heat oil in saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in chili powder and flour. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomato sauce and broth. Whisk until smooth.
Add cumin, garlic powder, oregano, and salt.
Simmer 10 minutes until thickened.

notes: Use on enchiladas, quesadillas, burritos, or tacos.
Can add chipotle for smoky version.
Keeps refrigerated for 1 week.

recipes.title: Cheese Enchiladas
recipes.description: Traditional Mexican-inspired cheese enchiladas - simple, satisfying, and perfect for a family dinner everyone will love.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Spread 1/2 cup enchilada sauce in bottom of 9x13 baking dish.
Warm tortillas to make them pliable.
Fill each tortilla with cheese (and onion if using). Roll up.
Place seam-side down in dish. Pour remaining sauce over top.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake 20-25 minutes until bubbly. Garnish and serve.

notes: Warm tortillas so they don't crack when rolling.
Can add beans, ground beef, or chicken.
Top with crumbled cotija for authentic touch.

recipes.title: Lo Mein Noodles
recipes.description: Easy lo mein noodles ready in 15 minutes with simple ingredients and customizable with vegetables and spices.

ingredients.prep_note: bell pepper, cabbage, snap peas, etc.

instructions.text: Cook noodles according to package. Drain and set aside.
Whisk together both soy sauces, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar, ginger, and sriracha.
Heat oil in wok over high heat. Stir-fry vegetables 2-3 minutes.
Add noodles and sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Cook 2 more minutes. Serve immediately.

notes: Lo mein means 'stirred noodles' - noodles are tossed into stir-fry.
Add chicken, beef, shrimp, or tofu for protein.
Customize vegetables to your preference.

recipes.title: Pad See Ew (Thai Stir-Fried Noodles)
recipes.description: Delicious Thai noodle dish with wide rice noodles stir-fried in savory sauce with vegetables and your choice of protein.

instructions.text: If using dried noodles, soak in warm water until pliable.
Mix soy sauces, oyster sauce, and sugar for sauce.
Heat wok over high heat. Add oil and stir-fry protein until cooked. Set aside.
Scramble eggs in wok. Set aside.
Add more oil, stir-fry garlic 30 seconds. Add noodles.
Add sauce and toss. Let noodles caramelize slightly on wok.
Add broccoli, protein, and eggs. Toss and serve.

notes: Wide rice noodles caramelize better in the wok.
Chinese broccoli (gai lan) is traditional but regular broccoli works.
High heat is essential for proper wok cooking.

recipes.title: No-Fail Smoked Pulled Pork
recipes.description: The juiciest, most tender smoky pulled pork, perfect for tacos, sandwiches, and more.

instructions.text: Coat pork with mustard, then generously apply dry rub.
Let sit 1 hour or refrigerate overnight.
Heat smoker to 225°F.
Smoke pork for 4 hours, adding wood chips regularly.
Spritz with apple cider vinegar every hour after first 4 hours.
Continue smoking until internal temp reaches 195-205°F.
Rest 30 minutes, then pull apart with forks.

notes: The stall around 160°F is normal - be patient.
Can wrap in foil at 160°F to push through stall faster.
Rest is essential for juicy meat.

recipes.title: Oven Baked Ribs with Honey-Sriracha Glaze
recipes.description: Tender oven baked baby back ribs drenched in tangy honey-sriracha glaze. Super easy to make.

instructions.text: Remove membrane from back of ribs.
Apply dry rub generously on both sides.
Wrap in foil and bake at 300°F for 2-2.5 hours.
Mix honey, sriracha, soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic for glaze.
Unwrap ribs, brush with glaze.
Broil 3-5 minutes or grill to caramelize glaze.

notes: Internal temp should reach 145°F minimum.
Ribs are done when meat pulls back from bones.
Can use BBQ sauce instead of honey-sriracha.

recipes.title: Jamaican Jerk Seasoning
recipes.description: Homemade Jamaican jerk seasoning blend filled with piquant and aromatic spices. Perfect for chicken thighs and pork chops.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
Store in airtight container.
Use as dry rub or mix with oil and vinegar for wet marinade.

notes: Allspice is the key flavor in jerk seasoning.
Marinate meat 1-2 hours for best flavor.
Keeps for months in airtight container.

recipes.title: Adobo Seasoning
recipes.description: Staple seasoning blend in Latin American, Caribbean and Spanish cuisine. An all-purpose seasoning for rubs and marinades.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Store in airtight container.
Use on meats, vegetables, rice, beans, and more.

notes: Essential in Puerto Rican and Filipino cooking.
Use as all-purpose seasoning or marinade base.
Add citrus juice for wet marinade.

recipes.title: Chicken Wings Dry Rub
recipes.description: Personal wing dry rub using 13 different spices for vibrant, bold flavor that takes wings to a whole new level.

instructions.text: Mix all spices together in a bowl.
Pat wings dry and coat generously with rub.
Let sit 30 minutes or refrigerate overnight.
Bake, grill, fry, or smoke wings as desired.

notes: Works for any cooking method.
Brown sugar helps with caramelization.
Adjust cayenne for desired heat.

recipes.title: Carnitas (Mexican Pulled Pork)
recipes.description: The ultimate Mexican pulled pork with seasoned pork shoulder cooked low and slow in lard, orange juice and milk until fall-apart tender. Perfect for tacos.

instructions.text: Season pork chunks generously with salt, cumin, and oregano.
Place pork in large pot with lard, orange juice, milk, onion, garlic, and bay leaves.
Bring to simmer over medium heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover partially, and cook 3-4 hours until tender.
Shred pork and crisp in hot skillet or under broiler.
Serve in tacos with salsa, onion, and cilantro.

notes: Originated in Michoacán, Mexico.
Lard is traditional but oil works too.
Crisping the edges after shredding is essential.

recipes.title: Beef Barbacoa
recipes.description: Tender shredded beef seasoned with ancho, guajillo, and chipotle peppers, cooked low and slow until juicy and tender.

instructions.text: Toast dried chiles in dry skillet. Soak in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend soaked chiles, chipotles, broth, vinegar, garlic, and spices until smooth.
Place beef in slow cooker. Pour sauce over.
Cook on low 8 hours until fall-apart tender.
Shred beef and mix with cooking liquid.
Serve in tacos, burritos, or over rice.

notes: Can also use beef cheek or brisket.
The three-chili blend creates complex flavor.
Chipotle adds smoky heat.

recipes.title: Carne Asada
recipes.description: Restaurant-style grilled steak with juicy citrus-garlic marinade for tender, smoky meat. Perfect for tacos or burritos.

instructions.text: Whisk lime juice, orange juice, olive oil, garlic, jalapeño, cumin, and cilantro.
Pour marinade over steak. Refrigerate at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Remove steak from marinade. Pat dry and season with salt and pepper.
Grill over high heat 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice against the grain.

notes: Carne asada means 'grilled meat' in Spanish.
Skirt steak is traditional but flank works well.
Slice thin against the grain for tender bites.

recipes.title: Pozole Rojo (Mexican Red Posole)
recipes.description: Comforting Mexican soup loaded with shredded pork and hominy, spiced with mild, vibrant red chilies and lots of toppings.

instructions.text: Toast dried chiles in dry skillet. Soak in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend soaked chiles with 1 cup broth until smooth.
Simmer pork in remaining broth with onion and garlic until tender, about 1.5 hours.
Shred pork and return to pot.
Add chile sauce, hominy, oregano, and cumin. Simmer 30 minutes.
Serve with shredded cabbage, radishes, oregano, lime, and tortilla chips.

notes: Traditional Mexican celebration dish.
Toppings are essential - don't skip them!
Can use chicken instead of pork.

recipes.title: Chili Verde (Pork Chile Verde)
recipes.description: Tender pork shoulder cooked low and slow in a rich verde sauce of roasted tomatillos, poblanos, and jalapeño peppers.

instructions.text: Roast tomatillos, poblanos, jalapeños, and onion under broiler until charred.
Blend roasted vegetables with garlic and cilantro until smooth.
Season pork with salt, cumin, and oregano. Brown in oil in large pot.
Add verde sauce and broth. Bring to simmer.
Cover and cook 2-3 hours until pork is tender.
Serve over rice or in tortillas with sour cream.

notes: Roasting the vegetables adds depth of flavor.
Can make in slow cooker on low for 8 hours.
Add more jalapeños for extra heat.

recipes.title: Kimchi
recipes.description: Homemade Korean spicy fermented vegetables with ingredient swaps so you can make it your own way.

instructions.text: Cut cabbage into 2-inch pieces. Toss with salt and let sit 2 hours.
Rinse cabbage well and squeeze out excess water.
Mix gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, and sugar to make paste.
Toss cabbage, green onions, and radish with paste. Pack into jar.
Press down to remove air. Leave 1 inch headspace.
Let ferment at room temperature 3-7 days, pressing down daily.
Refrigerate when tangy to your liking.

notes: Gochugaru is essential - it's not the same as regular red pepper flakes.
Use gochujang instead of gochugaru for different flavor.
Fermentation time affects sourness - longer = tangier.

recipes.title: Kimchi Fried Rice (Kimchi Bokkeumbap)
recipes.description: Popular Korean dish of kimchi stir-fried with rice and vegetables, flavored with gochujang and soy sauce, finished with sesame oil.

instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in large skillet or wok over high heat.
Add kimchi and stir-fry 2-3 minutes.
Add rice, gochujang, soy sauce, and kimchi juice. Stir-fry 5 minutes.
Drizzle with sesame oil and toss.
Top with fried eggs and green onions. Serve immediately.

notes: Use day-old rice for best texture.
Add protein like spam, bacon, or pork belly.
The runny egg yolk mixed in is essential.

recipes.title: Caribbean-Style Mango-Habanero Hot Sauce
recipes.description: Caribbean-inspired hot sauce with habanero peppers, velvety mango, vinegar, honey, and allspice. Great on grilled meats and seafood.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 15-20 minutes.
Let cool slightly.
Blend until smooth.
Strain if desired for smoother consistency.
Bottle and refrigerate.

notes: Perfect balance of sweet mango and fiery habanero.
Allspice adds Caribbean authenticity.
Great on jerk chicken, pulled pork, and fish tacos.

recipes.title: Pineapple-Habanero Hot Sauce
recipes.description: Sweet pineapple balanced with spicy habanero peppers and cilantro. Perfect for dashing over meals or spicing up cocktails.

instructions.text: Combine pineapple, habaneros, vinegar, and garlic in saucepan.
Simmer 10-15 minutes until pineapple softens.
Add cilantro and salt.
Blend until smooth.
Bottle and refrigerate.

notes: Cilantro adds fresh brightness.
Perfect for Bloody Marys and margaritas.
Adjust habaneros for desired heat.

recipes.title: Gochujang Sauce
recipes.description: 5-ingredient gochujang sauce that's easy to make and done in minutes. Perfect for stir-fries, rice bowls, and noodles.

instructions.text: Whisk all ingredients together until smooth.
Adjust sweetness and heat to taste.
Use immediately or refrigerate.

notes: Gochujang is Korean fermented red chili paste.
Add minced garlic for extra flavor.
Great as dipping sauce, marinade, or stir-fry sauce.

recipes.title: Salsa Verde (Mexican Green Salsa)
recipes.description: Traditional Mexican green salsa with roasted tomatillos, jalapeños, and fresh cilantro. Tangy, spicy, and incredibly versatile.

instructions.text: Roast tomatillos and jalapeños under broiler or on grill until charred.
Add to blender with onion, garlic, cilantro, lime juice, and salt.
Blend until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning.

notes: Roasting adds depth - don't skip it!
Remove jalapeño seeds for milder salsa.
Keeps refrigerated for 1 week.

recipes.title: Taco Soup
recipes.description: Chunky, hearty taco soup with tomatoes, ground beef, beans, chilies, and taco seasonings. All the flavor of tacos in a bowl.

instructions.text: Brown ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add tomatoes, beans, corn, green chiles, and broth.
Stir in taco seasoning, cumin, and chili powder.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with tortilla chips, sour cream, cheese, and fresh cilantro.

notes: Can use ground turkey instead of beef.
Great for meal prep - freezes well.
Top with avocado, jalapeños, or hot sauce.

recipes.title: Hot and Sour Soup
recipes.description: Classic Chinese Sichuan soup with pork and tofu in a spiced broth with silky egg ribbons. Hot, tangy, and deeply satisfying.

instructions.text: Bring broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add pork, tofu, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots. Simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in vinegar, soy sauce, white pepper, and chili oil.
Add cornstarch slurry and stir until thickened.
Slowly drizzle in beaten eggs while stirring gently.
Remove from heat, drizzle with sesame oil, and garnish with green onions.

notes: Adjust vinegar and pepper to taste for your preferred hot-sour balance.
Shiitake mushrooms can substitute for wood ear.
For extra heat, add more chili oil or white pepper.

recipes.title: Stuffed Pepper Soup
recipes.description: All the flavors of stuffed peppers in soup form - bell peppers, ground meat, rice, and tomatoes in a savory broth.

instructions.text: Brown ground beef in a large pot. Drain excess fat.
Add bell peppers, onion, and garlic. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth, Italian seasoning, and paprika.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in cooked rice and heat through.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with shredded cheese if desired.

notes: Add rice at the end so it doesn't get mushy.
Use a mix of colored peppers for visual appeal.
Can use ground turkey or Italian sausage.

recipes.title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
recipes.description: Hearty soup loaded with shredded chicken, black beans, corn, and peppers, topped with crispy tortilla strips.

instructions.text: Poach chicken in broth until cooked through. Remove and shred.
Sauté onion, jalapeños, and garlic until softened.
Add to broth along with tomatoes, beans, corn, cumin, and chili powder.
Add shredded chicken back to pot and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in lime juice and cilantro.
Fry or bake tortilla strips until crispy.
Serve soup topped with tortilla strips, avocado, sour cream, and cheese.

notes: Use rotisserie chicken for a shortcut.
Make tortilla strips extra crispy by frying in oil.
Add more jalapeños for extra heat.

recipes.title: Spicy Black Bean Soup
recipes.description: Creamy, hearty black bean soup with bold spices and just the right amount of heat. Perfect weeknight meal.

instructions.text: Sauté onion, bell pepper, jalapeño, and garlic in olive oil until softened.
Add cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute.
Add black beans and broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Blend half the soup until smooth, then return to pot.
Stir in lime juice, season with salt and pepper.
Serve with sour cream, cilantro, and tortilla chips.

notes: Partially blending gives the perfect creamy-chunky texture.
Add diced ham or bacon for extra flavor.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Gochujang Chicken
recipes.description: Quick and easy Korean-style chicken with a spicy-sweet gochujang sauce. Ready in just 10 minutes.

instructions.text: Mix gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 4-5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, cook 30 seconds.
Pour in sauce and toss to coat. Cook until sauce thickens.
Garnish with sesame seeds and green onions. Serve over rice.

notes: Gochujang is Korean fermented chili paste - find it in Asian markets.
Adjust gochujang amount for your heat preference.
Great for meal prep bowls.

recipes.title: Chicken Vindaloo
recipes.description: Classic Indian curry known for its spicy and tangy flavor. A bold dish with Portuguese-influenced spices.

instructions.text: Blend dried chilies with vinegar to make a paste.
Mix cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, and cinnamon.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds until they pop.
Add onions and cook until golden, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, cook 2 minutes.
Add spice mixture and chili-vinegar paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add chicken and brown on all sides.
Stir in tomato paste and water. Cover and simmer 25-30 minutes.
Adjust salt and serve with basmati rice or naan.

notes: Vindaloo gets its name from 'vinho e alho' (wine and garlic) from Portuguese influence.
Use ghost pepper flakes for extreme heat.
Better the next day as flavors develop.

recipes.title: Hunan Chicken
recipes.description: Iconic Chinese stir fry with lightly pan-fried chicken and vegetables in a spicy Hunan sauce. Ready in 15 minutes.

instructions.text: Mix soy sauce, rice wine, broth, and chili paste for the sauce.
Heat oil in wok over high heat until smoking.
Add chicken and stir-fry until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add more oil, then dried chilies, garlic, and ginger. Stir 30 seconds.
Add vegetables and stir-fry 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return chicken to wok, add sauce, and toss to coat.
Add cornstarch slurry and stir until sauce thickens.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

notes: Hunan cuisine is known for being spicier than Szechuan.
Don't eat the whole dried chilies - they're for flavor.
Have all ingredients prepped before you start - it goes fast.

recipes.title: Buldak (Korean Fire Chicken)
recipes.description: Popular Korean street food - chicken cooked in a fiery gochujang sauce, often topped with melty cheese. Intensely spicy and addictive.

instructions.text: Mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, rice wine, honey, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
Marinate chicken in sauce for at least 30 minutes (or overnight).
Cook chicken and sauce in a skillet over medium-high heat until chicken is cooked through.
Transfer to an oven-safe dish, top with mozzarella if using.
Broil until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds. Serve with rice.

notes: Buldak means 'fire chicken' - it's meant to be very spicy!
The cheese helps tame the heat.
Add rice cakes (tteok) for a more authentic version.

recipes.title: Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.description: Ultimate Chinese stir fry with wok-fried chicken, vegetables, and peanuts in a delicious spicy sauce. Features the unique numbing sensation of Sichuan peppercorns.

instructions.text: Mix soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin, sesame oil, and sugar for the sauce.
Heat oil in wok over high heat. Toast Sichuan peppercorns briefly, then remove.
Add dried chilies and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Add garlic, ginger, and white parts of green onions. Stir 30 seconds.
Return chicken to wok, add sauce and peanuts.
Add cornstarch slurry and stir until sauce thickens.
Garnish with green onion tops and serve over rice.

notes: Sichuan peppercorns create a unique numbing sensation (ma la).
Don't eat the whole dried chilies unless you want extreme heat.
Cashews can substitute for peanuts.

recipes.title: Jamaican Curry Chicken
recipes.description: Ultimate Caribbean comfort food - chicken seasoned with Jamaican curry powder and simmered in creamy curry sauce.

instructions.text: Season chicken with 2 tbsp curry powder, salt, and pepper. Let marinate 30 minutes.
Brown chicken in oil on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onion until softened. Add garlic, remaining curry powder, and allspice.
Add scotch bonnet (whole for mild, minced for hot) and thyme.
Add potatoes, coconut milk, and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to pot. Cover and simmer 30-40 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Remove scotch bonnet if used whole. Serve over rice and peas.

notes: Jamaican curry powder is different from Indian - it's more yellow and uses different spices.
Keep the scotch bonnet whole for flavor without extreme heat.
Serve with rice and peas, fried plantains, or hard dough bread.

recipes.title: Jalapeño Popper Dip
recipes.description: All the flavors of jalapeño poppers in an easy, creamy, baked dip with a crunchy topping.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise, cheddar, Parmesan, jalapeños, and garlic.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Spread into a baking dish.
Combine panko with melted butter, sprinkle on top.
Bake 15 minutes until bubbly and golden.
Serve hot with tortilla chips, crackers, or vegetables.

notes: Add crumbled bacon for extra flavor.
Use pickled jalapeños for a tangier version.
Can be made ahead and refrigerated - add 5 minutes to baking time.

recipes.title: Queso Dip
recipes.description: Perfect gooey cheese dip with jalapeños, tomatoes, and spices. Easy to make and always a crowd pleaser.

instructions.text: Heat milk in a saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add American cheese and stir until melted.
Add cheddar cheese gradually, stirring constantly.
Stir in tomatoes with chiles, jalapeños, garlic powder, cumin, and cayenne.
Continue stirring until smooth and heated through.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

notes: Use block cheese and shred it yourself - pre-shredded has anti-clumping agents.
Keep warm in a slow cooker on low setting.
Add cooked ground beef or chorizo for a heartier version.

recipes.title: Bacon Jalapeño Popper Dip
recipes.description: Loaded jalapeño popper dip with crispy bacon, extra cheese, and the perfect amount of spice. Ultimate party appetizer.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, half the bacon, 1 cup cheddar, jalapeños, and garlic.
Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a baking dish, top with remaining cheddar.
Bake 15 minutes until bubbly.
Top with remaining bacon, green onions, and cilantro.
Serve with tortilla chips.

notes: Reserve some jalapeño slices for garnish.
Use thick-cut bacon for more texture.
Can add ranch seasoning for extra flavor.

recipes.title: Nacho Cheese Sauce
recipes.description: Quick and easy homemade nacho cheese sauce that tastes just like movie theater nachos. The secret ingredient is pickled jalapeño juice!

instructions.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth.
Cook until thickened, about 3-4 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Add cheeses and stir until melted.
Stir in jalapeño juice, garlic powder, paprika, and cayenne.
Serve immediately over nachos or as a dip.

notes: The pickled jalapeño juice is the secret to authentic flavor.
Add diced pickled jalapeños for extra kick.
Thin with more milk if sauce gets too thick.

recipes.title: Spicy Grilled Chicken Sandwich
recipes.description: Grilled chicken sandwich drenched in habanero hot sauce with smoked gouda and sautéed peppers.

instructions.text: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Grill chicken over medium-high heat until cooked through, about 6-7 minutes per side.
Brush with habanero hot sauce during last minute of cooking.
Top with smoked gouda and let melt.
Sauté peppers and onion in olive oil until softened.
Assemble sandwiches: bun, chicken, sautéed peppers, lettuce, tomato.
Drizzle with more hot sauce if desired.

notes: Can use any habanero-based hot sauce.
Pound chicken to even thickness for even cooking.
Try with pepper jack cheese for a milder option.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Sandwich
recipes.description: Shredded chicken smothered in homemade buffalo sauce, topped with jalapeños and blue cheese crumbles.

instructions.text: Poach or bake chicken until cooked through. Shred with two forks.
Mix hot sauce, melted butter, and garlic powder for buffalo sauce.
Toss shredded chicken with buffalo sauce.
Toast brioche buns.
Build sandwiches: bun, lettuce, buffalo chicken, jalapeños, blue cheese.
Drizzle with ranch dressing and serve.

notes: Add ghost pepper flakes for extra heat.
Use rotisserie chicken for a quick shortcut.
Substitute blue cheese with ranch if preferred.

recipes.title: Spicy Meatball Sub Sandwiches
recipes.description: Classic meatball sub with seasoned beef meatballs seared then slow-cooked in spicy habanero-tomato sauce.

instructions.text: Mix ground beef, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, half the garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Form into 18-24 meatballs.
Brown meatballs in a skillet on all sides. Transfer to slow cooker.
Make sauce: combine crushed tomatoes, remaining garlic, habanero, and onion.
Pour sauce over meatballs. Cook on low 4 hours or high 2 hours.
Place meatballs and sauce on sub rolls, top with provolone.
Broil briefly to melt cheese. Serve hot.

notes: Use a mix of beef and pork for more flavor.
Adjust habanero amount for your heat tolerance.
Meatballs can be made ahead and frozen.

recipes.title: Muffaletta Sandwich
recipes.description: Ultimate New Orleans sandwich piled high with Italian meats, cheese, and a homemade spicy olive salad.

instructions.text: Make olive salad: combine olives, giardiniera, roasted peppers, olive oil, vinegar, garlic, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes. Let marinate at least 30 minutes.
Slice muffaletta bread horizontally.
Spread olive salad generously on both cut sides.
Layer meats and cheese on bottom half.
Replace top, press gently, and wrap tightly.
Let rest 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Cut into wedges and serve.

notes: Make the olive salad a day ahead for best flavor.
If you can't find muffaletta bread, use a round Italian loaf.
Add hot giardiniera for extra spice.

recipes.title: Cuban Sandwich
recipes.description: Ultimate Cuban sandwich with marinated roast pork, sliced ham, Swiss cheese, yellow mustard, and pickles, pressed until crispy.

instructions.text: Marinate pork in orange juice, lime juice, garlic, cumin, and oregano for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Roast pork at 350°F (175°C) for 3-4 hours until tender. Shred or slice.
Slice Cuban bread horizontally, spread mustard on both sides.
Layer: roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles.
Close sandwiches, butter the outside.
Press in a panini press or heavy skillet until bread is crispy and cheese melts.
Cut diagonally and serve hot.

notes: The mojo marinade is essential for authentic flavor.
Use leftover roast pork or buy pre-made pernil.
Must be pressed - the crispy exterior is key.

recipes.title: Penne Arrabbiata
recipes.description: Spicy Italian pasta with garlic, chili flakes, and a rich tomato sauce. Arrabbiata means 'angry' in Italian - your taste buds are in for a ride!

instructions.text: Cook penne in salted water according to package directions. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Heat olive oil over medium heat. Add garlic and red pepper flakes, cook 1-2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Drain pasta and add to sauce. Toss to coat, adding pasta water if needed.
Stir in parsley and serve with Parmesan.

notes: Use more red pepper flakes for extra heat.
San Marzano tomatoes give the best flavor.
Fresh hot peppers can be added for even more kick.

recipes.title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
recipes.description: Classic Italian pasta with spicy tomato sauce, guanciale, and pecorino. A spicy pasta lover's dream from the town of Amatrice.

instructions.text: Cook guanciale in olive oil until crispy. Remove and set aside.
Add red pepper flakes to the fat, then add wine and reduce.
Add tomatoes and simmer 15-20 minutes.
Cook bucatini until al dente. Reserve pasta water.
Toss pasta with sauce, adding pasta water if needed.
Add guanciale back, toss with pecorino and black pepper.

notes: Guanciale is cured pork jowl - pancetta or bacon can substitute.
Use the best quality tomatoes you can find.
Traditional recipe uses no garlic or onion.

recipes.title: Shrimp Fra Diavolo
recipes.description: Italian-American classic of shrimp in a fiery tomato sauce. Fra Diavolo means 'brother devil' - this sauce lives up to its name!

instructions.text: Season shrimp with salt and pepper. Sear in olive oil until pink. Remove and set aside.
Add garlic, red pepper flakes, and fresh chili to the pan. Cook 1 minute.
Add wine and reduce by half.
Add tomatoes and simmer 10-15 minutes.
Cook linguine until al dente.
Return shrimp to sauce, heat through.
Toss with pasta and basil. Serve immediately.

notes: Don't overcook the shrimp - they cook quickly in the hot sauce.
Add calabrian chili paste for authentic Italian heat.
Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.

recipes.title: Creamy Cajun Chicken Pasta
recipes.description: Seared chicken breast in a creamy, spicy Cajun sauce tossed with pasta. Easy weeknight dinner with huge flavor.

instructions.text: Season chicken with 1 tbsp Cajun seasoning. Sear in olive oil until cooked through. Set aside.
Sauté bell peppers and onion in butter until softened.
Add garlic and remaining Cajun seasoning, cook 1 minute.
Add cream and bring to a simmer. Stir in Parmesan until melted.
Cook pasta until al dente.
Add pasta and chicken to sauce. Toss to coat.
Garnish with parsley and serve.

notes: Add andouille sausage for extra Cajun flavor.
Use half-and-half for a lighter version.
Make your own Cajun seasoning with paprika, cayenne, garlic, onion powder, oregano, and thyme.

recipes.title: Pastalaya
recipes.description: Cajun pasta dish with all your favorite jambalaya ingredients, but with pasta instead of rice. Louisiana comfort food at its finest.

instructions.text: Brown andouille in a large pot. Remove and set aside.
Season chicken with Cajun seasoning, cook in the same pot. Set aside.
Sauté the holy trinity (onion, celery, bell pepper) until softened.
Add garlic, tomatoes, broth, and remaining seasoning. Bring to a boil.
Add pasta and cook until almost tender, stirring often.
Return sausage and chicken. Add shrimp and cook until pink.
Stir in hot sauce, top with green onions.

notes: The pasta absorbs all that flavorful Cajun broth.
Can omit shrimp for a meat-only version.
Adjust Cajun seasoning and hot sauce to your heat preference.

recipes.title: Cajun Shrimp Pasta
recipes.description: Succulent shrimp and pasta in a creamy, spicy tomato sauce with Cajun spices. Easy to make and perfectly spiced.

instructions.text: Season shrimp with half the Cajun seasoning.
Sauté shrimp in butter until pink. Remove and set aside.
Add garlic to pan, cook 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes and remaining Cajun seasoning. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add cream and bring to a simmer. Stir in Parmesan.
Cook fettuccine until al dente.
Add pasta and shrimp to sauce. Toss and serve with parsley.

notes: Don't overcook the shrimp - they'll finish in the sauce.
Add a splash of white wine for extra depth.
Serve with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Spicy Noodles
recipes.description: Asian-style noodles loaded with chili-garlic flavor, stir-fried in a vibrant, fiery sauce. Ready in just 10 minutes!

instructions.text: Cook noodles according to package. Drain and rinse.
Mix soy sauce, chili garlic sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sugar.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add garlic and ginger, stir 30 seconds.
Add noodles and sauce. Toss vigorously to coat.
Top with green onions and sesame seeds.

notes: Add protein: chicken, shrimp, or tofu.
Throw in vegetables: bok choy, broccoli, snap peas.
Adjust chili garlic sauce for your heat preference.

recipes.title: Mexican Pizza
recipes.description: Layered with seasoned taco meat, refried beans, enchilada sauce, and lots of cheese. A homemade Taco Bell-style classic.

instructions.text: Brown ground beef with taco seasoning. Drain fat.
Fry tortillas in oil until crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Spread refried beans on 4 tortillas.
Top with seasoned beef, then place another tortilla on top.
Spread enchilada sauce on top, then add cheese.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 8-10 minutes until cheese melts.
Top with tomatoes, olives, and green onions.

notes: Can air fry tortillas instead of deep frying.
Add jalapeños for extra heat.
Customize toppings: sour cream, guacamole, hot sauce.

recipes.title: Birria Pizza
recipes.description: Fusion of Mexican birria and Italian pizza with tender slow-cooked beef, melted cheese, and flavorful consomé for dipping.

instructions.text: Toast dried chiles in a dry pan. Cover with hot water and soak 20 minutes.
Blend chiles with some soaking liquid, onion, garlic, cumin, and oregano.
Brown beef in a Dutch oven. Add chile sauce, broth, and bay leaves.
Simmer covered for 2.5-3 hours until beef is tender. Shred meat.
Strain and reserve the consomé.
Stretch pizza dough, brush with some consomé fat.
Top with cheese and shredded birria meat.
Bake at 475°F (245°C) for 12-15 minutes.
Top with cilantro, serve with consomé for dipping.

notes: The consomé dip is essential - don't skip it!
Can use leftover birria meat from tacos.
Add Oaxacan cheese for extra stretch.

recipes.title: BBQ Chicken Pizza
recipes.description: Loaded with seasoned chicken, melty mozzarella, barbecue sauce, and roasted jalapeños for a spicy kick.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C) with a pizza stone if you have one.
Toss shredded chicken with half the BBQ sauce.
Stretch dough and brush with olive oil.
Spread remaining BBQ sauce over dough.
Top with cheese, chicken, onion, and jalapeños.
Bake 12-15 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbly.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

notes: Use rotisserie chicken for a quick shortcut.
Try different BBQ sauces - chipotle or habanero BBQ add extra heat.
Add bacon for even more flavor.

recipes.title: Homemade Pizza Sauce
recipes.description: Flavorful pizza sauce with tomatoes, garlic, jalapeños, and red pepper flakes with just a touch of sweetness.

instructions.text: Sauté onion, jalapeño, and garlic in olive oil until softened.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, basil, red pepper flakes, sugar, and salt.
Simmer 20-30 minutes until thickened.
Blend until smooth if desired, or leave chunky.
Cool before using on pizza.

notes: Can use San Marzano tomatoes for best flavor.
Freeze in portions for quick pizza making.
Adjust jalapeño and red pepper flakes for your heat preference.

recipes.title: Classic Chili
recipes.description: The best homemade chili with ground beef, beans, fire roasted tomatoes, and the perfect blend of chili seasonings.

instructions.text: Brown ground beef in a large pot. Drain excess fat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, and cayenne.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, beans, and broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 45-60 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with sour cream, cheese, onions, and crackers.

notes: Better the next day after flavors develop.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.
Add extra cayenne or hot sauce for more heat.

recipes.title: Texas Chili
recipes.description: Authentic Texas-style chili con carne - no beans, no tomatoes, just meat simmered in a rich dried chile sauce. More like a hearty beef stew.

instructions.text: Toast dried chiles in a dry pan until fragrant. Cover with hot water and soak 20 minutes.
Blend soaked chiles with 1 cup soaking liquid until smooth.
Brown beef in batches in bacon fat. Set aside.
Sauté onion until softened. Add garlic, cumin, and oregano.
Add chile paste, broth, and beef. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 2-2.5 hours until beef is tender.
Mix masa harina with a little water, stir into chili to thicken.
Season with salt and serve.

notes: True Texas chili has NO beans or tomatoes.
The dried chile combination is key - adjust for your heat preference.
Serve with saltine crackers, raw onion, and pickled jalapeños.

recipes.title: Brisket Chili
recipes.description: Hearty chili bursting with fire-roasted tomatoes, flavorful spices, and tender chopped brisket. Ultimate comfort food.

instructions.text: Season brisket cubes with salt, pepper, and half the chili powder.
Brown brisket in batches in oil. Set aside.
Sauté onion and jalapeños until softened. Add garlic.
Add remaining spices and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, broth, beer (if using), and brisket.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 2-2.5 hours.
Season to taste and serve with your favorite toppings.

notes: Low and slow is key for tender brisket.
Use leftover smoked brisket for even more flavor.
Dark beer adds depth - stout or porter work great.

recipes.title: Three Bean Chili
recipes.description: Easy to make and huge on flavor with ground beef and spicy chorizo simmered with fire roasted tomatoes, spices, and lots of beans.

instructions.text: Brown ground beef and chorizo together. Drain excess fat.
Add onion and cook until softened. Add garlic.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, and oregano.
Add tomatoes, all three beans, and broth.
Bring to a boil, then simmer 30-45 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with toppings.

notes: Chorizo adds amazing flavor - don't skip it!
Can use any combination of beans you prefer.
Top with cheese, sour cream, and green onions.

recipes.title: Short Rib and Chorizo Chili
recipes.description: Award-winning chili loaded with tender beef short ribs simmered with spicy Mexican chorizo, fire roasted tomatoes, and perfect spices.

instructions.text: Season short ribs with salt, pepper, and half the chili powder.
Brown short ribs in oil on all sides. Set aside.
Brown chorizo, breaking it up as it cooks. Set aside with short ribs.
Sauté onion, poblanos, and jalapeños until softened. Add garlic.
Add remaining spices, cook 1 minute.
Add beer and scrape up any browned bits.
Add tomatoes, broth, short ribs, and chorizo. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 2.5-3 hours until short ribs are tender.

notes: This recipe has won chili cook-off awards!
Short ribs become incredibly tender after slow cooking.
The chorizo adds a spicy, rich depth of flavor.

recipes.title: Southwest Style Slow Cooker Chili
recipes.description: Slow cooker chili with roasted green chiles, ground beef, fire roasted tomatoes, and Southwest seasonings. Set it and forget it!

instructions.text: Brown ground beef in a skillet. Drain fat.
Add all ingredients to slow cooker and stir.
Cook on low 6-8 hours or high 3-4 hours.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.
Serve with toppings: cheese, sour cream, cilantro, tortilla chips.

notes: Roast your own poblanos or use canned green chiles.
The longer it cooks, the better the flavors develop.
Great for meal prep - freezes well.
